 "file_text": "# R7 Risk Assessment — Permission Control Plane (\"ultimate control\")\n\n## Purpose\nR7 was the deferred request to give the agent \"ultimate control\" over GitHub\noperations. This document records the risk assessment that policy requires before\nany permission boundary is changed, and describes the control plane that was\nimplemented instead of a blanket permission increase.\n\n## What was implemented\nA single, pure, auditable decision function — `evaluatePermissionPolicy` in\n`src/agent/policy.ts` — that every GitHub write step consults before acting\n(branch creation, commit, pull request). The default profile preserves the\nexisting least-privilege behaviour: commit to an isolated `forge/task-*` branch\nand open a reviewable PR. Nothing merges.\n\n### Profiles\n| Profile | Branch write | Commit | Open PR | Merge |\n| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |\n| `readonly` | no | no | no | no |\n| `sandbox` | yes | yes | no | no |\n| `review` (default) | yes | yes | yes | no |\n| `publish` | yes | yes | yes | no |\n\n`merge` is intentionally never granted by this module for any profile.\n\n### Controls\n- `FORGE_PERMISSION_PROFILE` selects the profile (default `review`).\n- `FORGE_REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL=true` caps the effective profile at `sandbox`,\n  so the agent may prepare a reviewed branch but cannot open a PR without a\n  human decision.\n- Only branches under `FORGE_ALLOWED_BRANCH_PREFIX` (default `forge/task-`) may\n  be pushed; `FORGE_FORBIDDEN_BRANCHES` (default `main,master`) can never be\n  pushed, even on the highest profile.\n- `FORGE_ALLOWED_REPOS` restricts which repositories may be acted on.\n- Caller consent (`allowPrCreation`) remains mandatory: no consent means no write.\n\n## Risk assessment\n- **Blast radius**: bounded to an isolated branch; the default branch is denied\n  by policy, not only by convention.\n- **Escalation risk**: broadening authority requires an explicit profile change\n  and (optionally) is blocked by the human-approval cap. There is no path by\n  which the agent widens its own authority.\n- **Merge risk**: eliminated — merge is not representable in any profile.\n- **Auditability**: the decision is a pure function with unit tests\n  (`tests/policy.test.ts`), and every mission logs the effective profile and reason.\n- **Secrets**: unchanged; no credentials are introduced or exposed.\n\n## Human sign-off\nEnabling anything above `sandbox` for unattended runs should be an explicit\noperator decision. The human-approval cap exists so that the safe default\nrequires no change to repository settings.\n",

 "old_content": "# Firstborn / Forge\n\nForge is the deterministic coding agent for the Firstborn project. It is designed to\nbe driven by a supervising controller (a human operator or a \"shared GPT\" orchestrator)\nover two stable interfaces: a GitHub Actions workflow and a local HTTP API.\n\nThis document is the integration contract. It defines how a controller submits work,\nwhat it gets back, and what evidence accompanies every claim.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What Forge does\n\nFor a single task Forge will:\n\n1. Validate the task definition and verify the target repository and base commit.\n2. Inspect the repository and load its persistent instructions (`AGENTS.md`).\n3. Ask a free, keyless model for a plan and an exact-anchor patch (see section 3).\n4. Apply the patch in an isolated branch/worktree (`forge/task-<id>-<run>`).\n5. Run the repository's checks (`npm ci`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `git diff --check`).\n6. Commit exactly the tested tree and, when authorized, open a pull request.\n7. Return a `TaskExecutionReport` with the requirements matrix, raw test results, and\n   any honest blocker.\n\nForge never rewrites architecture, touches secrets, or changes unrelated files.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Interfaces a controller can use\n\n### 2.1 GitHub Actions (primary, remote)\n\nThe workflow `.github/workflows/forge.yml` runs the agent. It has two triggers:\n\n- `workflow_dispatch` with inputs `task_id`, `task_title`, `task_desc`.\n- An issue labeled `forge-task` authored by the repository `OWNER` (`issues: [labeled]`).\n\nBoth call `npx tsx src/agent/forge-runner.ts`, which reads the task from environment\nvariables (`TASK_ID`, `TASK_TITLE`, `TASK_DESC`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`) and runs in\nstrict keyless mode (`FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true`).\n\nDispatch example:\n\n```bash\ngh workflow run forge.yml --repo <owner>/<repo> --ref main \\\n  -f task_id=\"add-field-x\" \\\n  -f task_title=\"Add field X\" \\\n  -f task_desc=\"Modify only src/types/agent.ts ... (requirements + acceptance criteria)\"\n```\n\nThe run uploads a `forge-evidence` artifact containing the `TaskExecutionReport` JSON\nand a preflight record.\n\n### 2.2 Local HTTP API (`server.ts`)\n\nStart the server with `npm start` (Express on `PORT`, default 3000). All task\nendpoints require a GitHub token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) that is validated\nagainst GitHub and checked against an allowlist.\n\n| Method | Path | Purpose |\n| :-- | :-- | :-- |\n| GET | `/api/health` | Liveness and active model/provider policy. |\n| GET | `/api/github/inspect?repo=owner/repo` | Real repository inspection. |\n| POST | `/api/tasks/run` | Submit and execute a task synchronously; returns the report. |\n| GET | `/api/tasks/:id` | Retrieve a previously stored report. |\n| POST | `/api/verify/check` | Re-run the verification checks. |\n| GET | `/api/coordination` | Returns `COORDINATION.md` for handoff context. |\n\nSubmit example:\n\n```bash\ncurl -sS -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/tasks/run \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\n    \"id\": \"add-field-x\",\n    \"title\": \"Add field X\",\n    \"description\": \"REQ-1 ... acceptance criteria ...\",\n    \"targetRepo\": \"madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn\",\n    \"targetBranch\": \"main\",\n    \"allowPrCreation\": true\n  }'\n```\n\n### 2.3 Configuration\n\n| Variable | Effect |\n| :-- | :-- |\n| `GITHUB_TOKEN` | Required for authenticated endpoints and for commits/PRs. |\n| `FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY` | `true` removes provider credentials and disables the Gemini fallback. |\n| `FORGE_ALLOWED_REPOS` | Comma-separated repository allowlist (default: this repo). |\n| `FORGE_ALLOWED_LOGINS` | Comma-separated operator allowlist (default: the owner). |\n| `PORT` | HTTP port for `server.ts` (default 3000). |\n\n---\n\n## 3. Model policy (keyless, capability-first)\n\nRequirement: Forge must operate with **no API keys**, using free public endpoints, and\nmust always try the **finest free model currently available** before degrading.\n\n- Primary path: the `freelm` router with keyless endpoints (Kilo Gateway, OVHcloud).\n  No key is required; Gemini is an optional fallback that is disabled in keyless-only mode.\n- Discovery and ranking: Forge enumerates the live candidate models, then requests the\n  top capability tier first (`chat:large` / `chat:best`, i.e. the large-tagged models),\n  and only steps down to `chat`, `chat:fast`, and `chat:small` when a stronger route\n  fails or returns no usable text.\n- Failover: `freelm` degrades internally first (rate-limit rotation, cooldowns,\n  benching retired/overloaded models) before Forge steps down an alias tier.\n- Transparency: every response records the chosen provider/model and the reason any\n  stronger route was skipped in `keylessRouteErrors`.\n\nObserved keyless routes include `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` (Kilo),\n`Meta-Llama-3.3-70B` and `gpt-oss-120b` (OVHcloud).\n\n---\n\n## 4. Task definition\n\n```ts\ninterface TaskDefinition {\n  id: string;              // stable task id, also the branch/evidence name\n  title: string;\n  description: string;     // requirements + objective acceptance criteria\n  targetRepo: string;      // \"owner/repo\", must be allowlisted\n  targetBranch: string;    // base branch, default \"main\"\n  createdAt: string;       // ISO-8601\n  author: string;\n  allowPrCreation: boolean;// false = commit locally only, no PR\n}\n```\n\nWrite the description as a numbered requirement list with testable acceptance\ncriteria, and name the exact files or scope Forge may touch. Precise, bounded\nrequests produce smaller and more reliable patches.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Report contract\n\n```ts\ninterface TaskExecutionReport {\n  taskId: string;\n  status: TaskStatus;\n  startTime: string;\n  endTime?: string;\n  baseCommitSha: string;\n  headCommitSha?: string;\n  branchName?: string;\n  prUrl?: string;\n  prNumber?: number;\n  modelInvoked: {\n    provider: string; model: string; callsCount: number;\n    fallbackUsed?: boolean; keylessRouteErrors?: string[];\n  };\n  requirements: TaskRequirement[];   // { id, description, acceptanceCriteria, status, evidence }\n  plannedChanges: FileChangePlan[];\n  testResults: TestExecutionResult[];// raw command, exitCode, stdout, stderr\n  logs: { timestamp: string; level: 'info'|'warn'|'error'; message: string }[];\n  errorMessage?: string;\n  blockerReason?: string;\n}\n```\n\n### Status semantics\n\n| Status | Meaning |\n| :-- | :-- |\n| `QUEUED` / `VALIDATING` / `INSPECTING` / `PLANNING` / `EDITING` / `TESTING` / `VERIFYING` | In-flight stages. |\n| `PR_OPENED` | Success: tested commit created and a pull request opened. |\n| `FAILED` | A test or validation genuinely failed; inspect `errorMessage`. |\n| `BLOCKED` | A required external capability is unavailable; inspect `blockerReason`. |\n| `CANCELLED` | Superseded or explicitly aborted. |\n\nA controller must treat `FAILED` and `BLOCKED` as distinct. `BLOCKED` means the work\nmay be sound but an external precondition is missing; never report it as success.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Evidence contract\n\nEvery claim in a report is backed by raw evidence:\n\n- `testResults[]` carries the exact command, exit code, and full stdout/stderr.\n- `npm run model:smoke` proves the keyless model path end to end.\n- On GitHub runs, the `forge-evidence` artifact holds the report JSON and preflight record.\n- Locally, reports are written to `.firstborn/evidence/<taskId>.json`.\n\nVerification commands (the same checks CI runs):\n\n```bash\nnpm ci\nnpm run lint          # tsc --noEmit\nnpm run build         # vite build\nnpm test              # node:test suites\nnpm run model:smoke   # keyless primary model smoke test\nnpm start             # boots the HTTP API\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Safety model\n\n- An exact-command registry with `shell: false`; no arbitrary shell execution.\n- Patch validation rejects path traversal, symlinks, and protected files, and requires\n  unique exact anchors.\n- Operator credentials are validated server-side against an allowlist and are never\n  logged; secrets are stripped from git subprocess environments.\n- Untrusted input (issue bodies, task text, model output) is treated as data, never as\n  instructions that can widen permissions.\n- Forge pushes only to isolated `forge/task-*` branches and never to the default branch.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Operational notes and caveats\n\nThese are verified facts about the current environment, useful when a controller\ninterprets results:\n\n- **Native in-workflow PR creation is enabled.** Forge opens its own pull requests from\n  Actions using `GITHUB_TOKEN`; PRs are authored by `github-actions[bot]` (e.g. #21, #25).\n  The repository setting \"Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests\" is on.\n- **`pull_request` checks run for bot branches.** Verification workflows triggered by\n  agent-created pull requests execute and pass; they are not gated behind manual approval\n  in the current configuration.\n- **The API token used for automation is a GitHub App installation token.** It cannot read\n  or change repository Actions settings (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions`\n  returns `403`), so those settings must be managed by a repository administrator.\n- **Free-tier variability.** Named free models change over time and are rate-limited; the\n  router adapts and always prefers the strongest available tier, but a specific model is\n  never guaranteed across runs.\n",

```
Here's where we stand now — I built the remaining items and drove the queue to a real end state.

## What I shipped (branch `feat/forge-controller-hardening`, PR #34, CI green)

**1. Capability-first keyless router (item a)** — `src/services/model.ts`
Now requests the **top capability tier first** (`chat:large`/`chat:best` → large-tagged models), degrading only on failure. Verified: `chat:large` → `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free` (120B) via kilo — stronger than the old `chat`-first pick.

**2. Controller-handoff README (item b)** — new `README.md`
The full integration contract: Actions + HTTP interfaces, model policy, task/report/evidence contracts, safety model, permission controls.

**3. R7 permission control plane — "ultimate control" (M5)** — new `src/agent/policy.ts`
A single pure, auditable decision function consulted **before every GitHub write** (branch, commit, PR):
- Profiles `readonly < sandbox < review (default) < publish`; **merge is never representable**; `main`/`master` denied by policy.
- `FORGE_REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL=true` caps the effective profile at `sandbox` for human sign-off.
- **Default equals the previous least-privilege behaviour** — I did not widen authority.
- Required risk assessment: `docs/R7_PERMISSION_RISK_ASSESSMENT.md`.

**4. Repository hygiene (M4)** — open PR queue **11 → 3**, each with a one-line disposition, **no unique content dropped** (#26's useful line folded into #34).

## Evidence (observed, not claimed)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm test` | **36/36** (was 27; +9 policy tests), exit 0 |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| `npm run model:smoke` | **PASS** (keyless, 120B nemotron via kilo) |
| CI `verify` on PR #34 | **success** |

Also caught and fixed a real defect you'd flagged the class of: `src/App.tsx` AC11/AC18 still claimed native PR creation was "externally blocked" — it isn't (PRs #21/#25 were authored by `github-actions[bot]`).

## Honest status: not yet 100%

**~90% of the stated goal; ~85% of the "ultimate agent" vision.**

What remains, and it's specific:
1. **Merge PR #34** — needs your merge authority (I don't auto-merge).
2. **M3** — wire `runStagedMission` into the live execute loop for durable multi-stage missions (the engine exists and is tested; the live wiring is the last roadmap item). This is the real remaining engineering work.
3. **#10 remaining id** — nothing else structural.

Two decisions only you can make:
- **"Three long models"** — do you want exactly three *pinned* providers, or is "always the finest free model available" (what I built) the actual requirement? Today the keyless pool is Kilo + OVH with many models each.
- **R7 default** — I kept it at `review` (least privilege). If you want the agent to run fully unattended with PR authority, set `FORGE_PERMISSION_PROFILE=publish`; if you want a mandatory human gate, set `FORGE_REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL=true`.

Say "merge #34" and "do M3," and I'll take the last item across the line. PR #34: https://github.com/madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn/pull/34
```

Each find string must occur\n * exactly once, so an ambiguous or missing anchor is a hard, reported error\n * rather than a silent partial edit.\n */\nexport function applyExactEdits(content: string, edits: { find: string; replace: string }[]): EditApplication {\n  let current = content;\n  for (const edit of edits) {\n    if (!edit || typeof edit.find !== 'string' || edit.find.length === 0 || typeof edit.replace !== 'string') {\n      return { ok: false, content: current, error: 'Malformed exact-edit entry.' };\n    }\n    const first = current.indexOf(edit.find);\n    if (first < 0) {\n      return { ok: false, content: current, error: `Exact anchor not found: ${JSON.stringify(edit.find.slice(0, 100))}` };\n    }\n    const second = current.indexOf(edit.find, first + edit.find.length);\n    if (second >= 0) {\n      return { ok: false, content: current, error: `Anchor is ambiguous: ${JSON.stringify(edit.find.slice(0, 100))}` };\n    }\n    current = current.slice(0, first) + edit.replace + current.slice(first + edit.find.length);\n  }\n  return { ok: true, content: current };\n}\n\nexport interface MissionStage {\n  id: string;\n  /** File changes for this stage only. */\n  changes: FileChangePlan[];\n  /** Check command expected to verify this stage, if any. */\n  check?: string;\n}\n\nexport type StageStatus = 'APPLIED' | 'FAILED' | 'SKIPPED';\n\nexport interface StageOutcome {\n  id: string;\n  status: StageStatus;\n  problems: string[];\n  checkPassed?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface StagedMissionResult {\n  stages: StageOutcome[];\n  finalContents: Record<string, string>;\n  appliedStages: number;\n  completed: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Execute an ordered, bounded sequence of file-edit stages against a snapshot of\n * file contents. A stage is applied only after its anchors validate against the\n * cumulative contents; if a stage fails validation or its check fails, the\n * mission stops and every remaining stage is SKIPPED. This guarantees a failing\n * stage is never treated as success and that the final contents reflect only\n * validated, applied stages.\n */\nexport async function runStagedMission(\n  stages: MissionStage[],\n  initialContents: Record<string, string>,\n  runCheck?: (stage: MissionStage) => Promise<boolean>\n): Promise<StagedMissionResult> {\n  const contents: Record<string, string> = { ...initialContents };\n  const outcomes: StageOutcome[] = [];\n  let completed = true;\n\n  for (const stage of stages) {\n    const problems: string[] = [];\n    const nextContents: Record<string, string> = { ...contents };\n\n    for (const change of stage.changes) {\n      if (change.action === 'create') {\n        if (contents[change.path] !== undefined) {\n          problems.push(`${change.path}: stage marked existing file as create.`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        if (typeof change.content !== 'string' || change.content.length === 0) {\n          problems.push(`${change.path}: create needs content.`);\n          continue;\n        }\n        nextContents[change.path] = change.content;\n        continue;\n      }\n      if (change.action !== 'modify') {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: unsupported stage action \"${change.action}\".`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      const source = nextContents[change.path];\n      if (typeof source !== 'string') {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: source content was not supplied to validate the edit anchors.`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      const result = applyExactEdits(source, change.edits ?? []);\n      if (!result.ok) {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: ${result.error}`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      nextContents[change.path] = result.content;\n    }\n\n    if (problems.length > 0) {\n      outcomes.push({ id: stage.id, status: 'FAILED', problems });\n      completed = false;\n      // Mark every remaining stage SKIPPED.\n      for (const remaining of stages.slice(outcomes.length)) {\n        outcomes.push({ id: remaining.id, status: 'SKIPPED', problems: ['Not run: a prior stage failed.'] });\n      }\n      break;\n    }\n\n    Object.assign(contents, nextContents);\n\n    if (stage.check && runCheck) {\n      const checkPassed = await runCheck(stage);\n      if (!checkPassed) {\n        outcomes.push({ id: stage.id, status: 'FAILED', problems: [], checkPassed: false });\n        completed = false;\n        for (const remaining of stages.slice(outcomes.length)) {\n          outcomes.push({ id: remaining.id, status: 'SKIPPED', problems: ['Not run: a prior stage failed.'] });\n        }\n        break;\n      }\n      outcomes.push({ id: stage.id, status: 'APPLIED', problems: [], checkPassed: true });\n      continue;\n    }\n\n    outcomes.push({ id: stage.id, status: 'APPLIED', problems: [] });\n  }\n\n  return {\n    stages: outcomes,\n    finalContents: contents,\n    appliedStages: outcomes.filter((outcome) => outcome.status === 'APPLIED').length,\n    completed,\n  };\n}"

 "new_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport { TaskDefinition, TaskExecutionReport, FileChangePlan, RequirementEvidenceInput } from '../types/agent.ts';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { loadForgeLimits } from './limits.ts';\nimport { evaluatePermissionPolicy, loadPermissionConfig } from './policy.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport * as fs from 'fs/promises';\nimport * as path from 'path';\nimport * as os from 'os';\nimport { execFile } from 'child_process';\nimport { promisify } from 'util';\n\nconst execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);\n\n// Sensitive / Protected repository paths that Forge is prohibited from altering\nconst PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS = [\n  /^\\.git\\//i,\n  /^\\.env/i,\n  /^\\.github\\//i,\n  /^node_modules\\//i,\n  // Files executed by target checks must not be model-editable.\n  /(^|\\/)package(-lock)?\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)npm-shrinkwrap\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)\\.npmrc$/i,\n  /^vite\\.config\\.[cm]?[jt]s$/i,\n  /^tsconfig[^/]*\\.json$/i,\n  /^scripts\\//i,\n];\n\n// Keep the total source context bounded for anonymous models with small context windows.\nconst MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS = 24000;\n\n// Anonymous models sometimes wrap otherwise valid JSON in Markdown fences.\n// Normalize only that wrapper; JSON.parse remains the strict structural validator.\nfunction parseModelJson(text: string): any {\n  let normalized = text.trim();\n  if (normalized.startsWith('```')) {\n    const firstLineEnd = normalized.indexOf('\\n');\n    if (firstLineEnd >= 0) normalized = normalized.slice(firstLineEnd + 1);\n    const trimmedEnd = normalized.trimEnd();\n    if (trimmedEnd.endsWith('```')) normalized = trimmedEnd.slice(0, -3);\n    normalized = normalized.trim();\n  }\n  return JSON.parse(normalized);\n}\n\n// --- R6 resilience primitives -------------------------------------------------\n\nexport type FailureClass = 'RETRYABLE' | 'FATAL';\n\n/**\n * Classify a runtime failure so callers can retry transient conditions and stop\n * on permanent ones. Deterministic and pure so it is unit-testable.\n */\nexport function classifyFailure(error: unknown): FailureClass {\n  const message = (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)).toLowerCase();\n  const status = (error as { status?: number })?.status;\n  if (status === 429 || status === 408 || (typeof status === 'number' && status >= 500)) return 'RETRYABLE';\n  if (/abort|timeout|timed out|econnreset|enotfound|socket hang up|fetch failed|rate limit|429|5\\d\\d/.test(message)) {\n    return 'RETRYABLE';\n  }\n  return 'FATAL';\n}\n\nexport interface BoundedRetryOptions {\n  attempts: number;\n  baseDelayMs?: number;\n  maxDelayMs?: number;\n  /** Injected sleep so tests never wait on wall-clock time. */\n  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  isRetryable?: (error: unknown) => boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run an async operation with bounded retries and exponential backoff. Never\n * loops unbounded, never retries a fatal classification, and reports the exact\n * number of attempts so the caller can log truthful evidence.\n */\nexport async function withBoundedRetry<T>(\n  operation: () => Promise<T>,\n  options: BoundedRetryOptions\n): Promise<{ ok: true; value: T; attempts: number } | { ok: false; error: unknown; attempts: number }> {\n  const attempts = Math.max(1, Math.floor(options.attempts));\n  const base = options.baseDelayMs ?? 250;\n  const max = options.maxDelayMs ?? 2000;\n  const sleep = options.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms)));\n  const retryable = options.isRetryable ?? ((error: unknown) => classifyFailure(error) === 'RETRYABLE');\n\n  let lastError: unknown;\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {\n    try {\n      return { ok: true, value: await operation(), attempts: attempt };\n    } catch (error) {\n      lastError = error;\n      if (attempt >= attempts || !retryable(error)) {\n        return { ok: false, error, attempts: attempt };\n      }\n      const delay = Math.min(max, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1));\n      await sleep(delay);\n    }\n  }\n  return { ok: false, error: lastError, attempts };\n}\n\nexport interface ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  ok: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  requirements: { id: string; description: string; acceptanceCriteria: string; checkCommands?: string[]; manualReviewNote?: string }[];\n  changes: FileChangePlan[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Deterministically validate and normalize a raw model plan. Malformed shapes\n * are reported as structured errors instead of throwing deep in the mapper, so\n * a single bad field cannot silently corrupt the report.\n */\nexport function validateModelPlanShape(raw: unknown): ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  const empty: ModelPlanShapeCheck = { ok: true, requirements: [], changes: [] };\n  if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan was not a JSON object.' };\n  }\n  const plan = raw as Record<string, unknown>;\n\n  if (plan.requirements !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.requirements)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"requirements\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n  if (plan.changes !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.changes)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"changes\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n\n  const requirements = (plan.requirements ?? []).map((req, index) => {\n    const item = (req ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id ? item.id : `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n      description: typeof item.description === 'string' ? item.description : '',\n      acceptanceCriteria: typeof item.acceptanceCriteria === 'string' ? item.acceptanceCriteria : '',\n      checkCommands: Array.isArray(item.checkCommands)\n        ? item.checkCommands.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && c.trim().length > 0)\n        : undefined,\n      manualReviewNote: typeof item.manualReviewNote === 'string' ? item.manualReviewNote : undefined,\n    };\n  });\n\n  const changes: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n  for (const change of (plan.changes ?? []) as unknown[]) {\n    const item = (change ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (typeof item.path !== 'string' || item.path.length === 0) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'A change is missing a \"path\".' };\n    }\n    if (!['create', 'modify', 'delete'].includes(String(item.action))) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has an invalid action \"${String(item.action)}\".` };\n    }\n    if (item.edits !== undefined && !Array.isArray(item.edits)) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has non-array edits.` };\n    }\n    changes.push({\n      path: item.path,\n      action: item.action as FileChangePlan['action'],\n      rationale: typeof item.rationale === 'string' ? item.rationale : '',\n      content: typeof item.content === 'string' ? item.content : undefined,\n      edits: Array.isArray(item.edits)\n        ? (item.edits as { find: string; replace: string }[])\n        : undefined,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, requirements, changes };\n}\n\n// Requested branch wins only when it is explicit and not the default; invalid\n// branches are resolved later (and fail closed) by the caller.\nexport function resolveTargetBranch(requested: string | undefined, defaultBranch: string): string {\n  const trimmed = requested?.trim();\n  return trimmed && trimmed !== defaultBranch ? trimmed : defaultBranch;\n}\n\n// A requirement is only PASS when a check named in its own acceptance criteria,\n// description, or explicit checkCommands actually passed. Unrelated green checks\n// cannot satisfy it, and a named-but-failing check yields FAIL, never PASS.\nexport function evaluateRequirementEvidence(\n  requirement: RequirementEvidenceInput,\n  results: { command: string; status: string; exitCode: number }[]\n): { status: 'PASS' | 'PENDING' | 'FAIL'; evidence: string } {\n  const attemptEvidence = results.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ');\n  const criterion = `${requirement.acceptanceCriteria ?? ''} ${requirement.description ?? ''}`.toLowerCase();\n\n  const matchesCommand = (command: string): boolean => {\n    const lower = command.toLowerCase();\n    const scriptName = lower === 'npm test' ? 'test' : lower.replace(/^npm run /, '');\n    return criterion.includes(lower) || criterion.includes(scriptName);\n  };\n\n  const explicit = (requirement.checkCommands ?? []).map((c) => c.toLowerCase());\n  const referencedChecks = results.filter((result) => {\n    const lower = result.command.toLowerCase();\n    return explicit.includes(lower) || matchesCommand(result.command);\n  });\n\n  const failed = referencedChecks.filter((result) => result.status !== 'PASSED');\n  if (failed.length > 0) {\n    return {\n      status: 'FAIL',\n      evidence: `Criterion-named check failed: ${failed.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ')}.`,\n    };\n  }\n  if (referencedChecks.length > 0) {\n    return {\n      status: 'PASS',\n      evidence: `Criterion-matched checks passed: ${referencedChecks.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ')}.`,\n    };\n  }\n  const manual = requirement.manualReviewNote ? ` Manual review: ${requirement.manualReviewNote}.` : ' Manual review required.';\n  return {\n    status: 'PENDING',\n    evidence: `No criterion-specific passing check was identified. Latest target-check attempt: ${attemptEvidence}.${manual}`,\n  };\n}\n\nexport class ForgeAgent {\n  private github: GitHubService;\n  private model: ModelService;\n  private testRunner: TestRunnerService;\n  private githubToken?: string;\n\n  constructor(githubToken?: string) {\n    this.githubToken = githubToken?.trim();\n    this.github = new GitHubService(githubToken);\n    this.model = new ModelService();\n    this.testRunner = new TestRunnerService();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Strict validation of generated patch paths and contents (Fixes AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n   */\n  private validatePatch(changes: FileChangePlan[]): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {\n    const limits = loadForgeLimits();\n    if (!Array.isArray(changes) || changes.length === 0) {\n      return { valid: false, error: 'Empty patch: No file changes proposed.' };\n    }\n    if (changes.length > limits.maxFilesPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured file ceiling: ${changes.length} > ${limits.maxFilesPerMission}.` };\n    }\n    const totalEdits = changes.reduce((sum, change) => sum + (Array.isArray(change.edits) ? change.edits.length : 0), 0);\n    if (totalEdits > limits.maxEditsPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured edit ceiling: ${totalEdits} > ${limits.maxEditsPerMission}.` };\n    }\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      // 1. Path format validation (must be relative, no traversal)\n      if (!change.path || typeof change.path !== 'string') {\n        return { valid: false, error: 'Malformed patch: Missing or non-string file path.' };\n      }\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      if (path.isAbsolute(change.path) || portablePath.startsWith('/') || normalizedPath === '..' || normalizedPath.startsWith('../') || normalizedPath.includes('/../')) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Security Boundary Violation: Directory traversal or absolute path detected: \"${change.path}\".` };\n      }\n\n      // 2. Protected files check\n      if (PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS.some((pat) => pat.test(normalizedPath))) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Security Boundary Violation: Modification of protected file or path is forbidden: \"${change.path}\".` };\n      }\n      change.path = normalizedPath; // commit exactly the path that was tested\n\n      // 3. Only create and modify are supported.` };\n      }\n      const hasContent = typeof change.content === 'string' && change.content.length > 0;\n      const hasEdits = Array.isArray(change.edits) && change.edits.length > 0\n        && change.edits.every((edit) => edit && typeof edit.find === 'string' && edit.find.length > 0 && typeof edit.replace === 'string');\n      if ((change.action === 'create' && !hasContent) || (change.action === 'modify' && !hasContent && !hasEdits)) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Invalid patch: \"${change.path}\" needs complete content for create or valid exact edits for modify.` };\n      }\n      const patchSize = hasContent ? Buffer.byteLength(change.content as string, 'utf-8') : Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(change.edits ?? Defaults preserve\n      // least privilege; broader capability must be enabled explicitly.\n      const permission = evaluatePermissionPolicy(\n        {\n          requestedPrCreation: task.allowPrCreation,\n          branchName,\n          targetBranch,\n          repo: `${owner}/${repo}`,\n        },\n        loadPermissionConfig(),\n      );\n\n      // Extract validated files with content\n      const filesToCommit = report.plannedChanges\n        .filter((c) => c.content && typeof c.content === 'string')\n        .map((c) => ({ path: c.path, content: c.content as string }));\n\n      // Fix AUD-20261012-02 Empty PR prevention: fail closed if no file contents are committed\n      if (filesToCommit.length === 0) {\n        report.status = 'FAILED';\n        report.errorMessage = 'Safety Block: Zero files with valid content to commit. Cannot open empty Pull Request.';\n        log('error', report.errorMessage);\n        return report;\n      }\n\n      if (!task.allowPrCreation) {\n        log('info', 'Task verified locally. Pull Request creation not authorized by caller.');\n        report.status = 'VERIFYING';\n      } else if (!permission.allowBranchWrite) {\n        report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n        report.blockerReason = `Permission policy denied GitHub write: ${permission.reason}`;\n        log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n      } else {\n        log('info', `Permission policy (${permission.effectiveProfile}): ${permission.reason}`);\n        log('info', `Creating or updating isolated branch ${branchName} at base SHA ${report.baseCommitSha}...`);\n        const branchRes = await this.github.createOrUpdateBranch(owner, repo, branchName, report.baseCommitSha);\n\n        if (!branchRes.success) {\n          log('warn', `Branch operation halted: ${branchRes.error}`);\n          report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n          report.blockerReason = `GitHub branch operation blocked: ${branchRes.error}`;\n        } else {\n          log('info', `Branch ${branchName} confirmed.`);\n\n          // Commit the actual patch files to the branch with base tree SHA resolution\n          log('info', `Committing ${filesToCommit.length} modified files to ${branchName}...`);\n          const commitRes = await this.github.commitChangesToBranch({\n            owner,\n            repo,\n            branchName,\n            baseCommitSha: report.baseCommitSha,\n            commitMessage: `[Forge] ${task.title}\\n\\nTask-ID: ${task.id}\\nRequirements: ${report.requirements.map(r => r.id).join(', ')}`,\n            files: filesToCommit,\n          });\n\n          if (commitRes.success && commitRes.headSha) {\n            report.headCommitSha = commitRes.headSha;\n            log('info', `Committed changes. Head SHA: ${report.headCommitSha}`);\n\n            // Open Pull Request with genuine head and base (requires 'review' profile)\n            log('info', 'Opening Pull Request on GitHub...');\n            if (!permission.allowOpenPr) {\n              report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n              report.blockerReason = `Permission policy withheld Pull Request: ${permission.reason}`;\n              log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n              return report;\n            }\n            const prRes = await this.github.openPullRequest({\n              owner,\n              repo,\n              title: `[Forge] ${task.title}`,\n              head: branchName,\n              base: targetBranch,\n              body: `### Forge Task Report: ${task.id}\n- **Base Commit**: \\`${report.baseCommitSha}\\`\n- **Head Commit**: \\`${report.headCommitSha}\\`\n- **Provider**: ${report.modelInvoked.provider}\n- **Model**: ${report.modelInvoked.model}\n- **Fallback Used**: ${report.modelInvoked.fallbackUsed ?? 'unknown'}\n- **Keyless Route Errors**: ${(report.modelInvoked.keylessRouteErrors ?? []).join(' | ') || 'none reported'}\n- **Status**: ${report.status}\n- **Tests**: ${report.testResults.map((r) => `${r.command}: ${r.status}`).join(', ')}\n`,\n            });\n\n            if (prRes.success) {\n              report.status = 'PR_OPENED';\n              report.prUrl = prRes.url;\n              report.prNumber = prRes.number;\n              log('info', `Pull Request opened: ${prRes.url}`);\n            } else {\n              report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n              report.blockerReason = `PR opening blocked: ${prRes.error}`;\n              log('warn', report.blockerReason);\n            }\n          } else {\n            log('warn', `Commit failed: ${commitRes.error}`);\n            report.status = 'BLOCKED';\n            report.blockerReason = `Git commit blocked: ${commitRes.error}`;\n          }\n        }\n      }\n\n      report.endTime = new Date().toISOString();\n      return report;\n    } catch (err: any) {\n      report.status = 'FAILED';\n      report.errorMessage = `Unhandled agent exception: ${err.message}`;\n      report.endTime = new Date().toISOString();\n      log('error', report.errorMessage);\n      return report;\n    }\n  }\n}\n",
 "new_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport { TaskDefinition, TaskExecutionReport, FileChangePlan, RequirementEvidenceInput } from '../types/agent.ts';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { loadForgeLimits } from './limits.ts';\nimport { evaluatePermissionPolicy, loadPermissionConfig } from './policy.ts';\nimport { traceEntry } from './mission-trace.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport * as fs from 'fs/promises';\nimport * as path from 'path';\nimport * as os from 'os';\nimport { execFile } from 'child_process';\nimport { promisify } from 'util';\n\nconst execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);\n\n// Sensitive / Protected repository paths that Forge is prohibited from altering\nconst PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS = [\n  /^\\.git\\//i,\n  /^\\.env/i,\n  /^\\.github\\//i,\n  /^node_modules\\//i,\n  // Files executed by target checks must not be model-editable.\n  /(^|\\/)package(-lock)?\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)npm-shrinkwrap\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)\\.npmrc$/i,\n  /^vite\\.config\\.[cm]?[jt]s$/i,\n  /^tsconfig[^/]*\\.json$/i,\n  /^scripts\\//i,\n];\n\n// Keep the total source context bounded for anonymous models with small context windows.\nconst MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS = 24000;\n\n// Anonymous models sometimes wrap otherwise valid JSON in Markdown fences.\n// Normalize only that wrapper; JSON.parse remains the strict structural validator.\nfunction parseModelJson(text: string): any {\n  let normalized = text.trim();\n  if (normalized.startsWith('```')) {\n    const firstLineEnd = normalized.indexOf('\\n');\n    if (firstLineEnd >= 0) normalized = normalized.slice(firstLineEnd + 1);\n    const trimmedEnd = normalized.trimEnd();\n    if (trimmedEnd.endsWith('```')) normalized = trimmedEnd.slice(0, -3);\n    normalized = normalized.trim();\n  }\n  return JSON.parse(normalized);\n}\n\n// --- R6 resilience primitives -------------------------------------------------\n\nexport type FailureClass = 'RETRYABLE' | 'FATAL';\n\n/**\n * Classify a runtime failure so callers can retry transient conditions and stop\n * on permanent ones. Deterministic and pure so it is unit-testable.\n */\nexport function classifyFailure(error: unknown): FailureClass {\n  const message = (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)).toLowerCase();\n  const status = (error as { status?: number })?.status;\n  if (status === 429 || status === 408 || (typeof status === 'number' && status >= 500)) return 'RETRYABLE';\n  if (/abort|timeout|timed out|econnreset|enotfound|socket hang up|fetch failed|rate limit|429|5\\d\\d/.test(message)) {\n    return 'RETRYABLE';\n  }\n  return 'FATAL';\n}\n\nexport interface BoundedRetryOptions {\n  attempts: number;\n  baseDelayMs?: number;\n  maxDelayMs?: number;\n  /** Injected sleep so tests never wait on wall-clock time. */\n  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  isRetryable?: (error: unknown) => boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run an async operation with bounded retries and exponential backoff. Never\n * loops unbounded, never retries a fatal classification, and reports the exact\n * number of attempts so the caller can log truthful evidence.\n */\nexport async function withBoundedRetry<T>(\n  operation: () => Promise<T>,\n  options: BoundedRetryOptions\n): Promise<{ ok: true; value: T; attempts: number } | { ok: false; error: unknown; attempts: number }> {\n  const attempts = Math.max(1, Math.floor(options.attempts));\n  const base = options.baseDelayMs ?? 250;\n  const max = options.maxDelayMs ?? 2000;\n  const sleep = options.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms)));\n  const retryable = options.isRetryable ?? ((error: unknown) => classifyFailure(error) === 'RETRYABLE');\n\n  let lastError: unknown;\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {\n    try {\n      return { ok: true, value: await operation(), attempts: attempt };\n    } catch (error) {\n      lastError = error;\n      if (attempt >= attempts || !retryable(error)) {\n        return { ok: false, error, attempts: attempt };\n      }\n      const delay = Math.min(max, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1));\n      await sleep(delay);\n    }\n  }\n  return { ok: false, error: lastError, attempts };\n}\n\nexport interface ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  ok: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  requirements: { id: string; description: string; acceptanceCriteria: string; checkCommands?: string[]; manualReviewNote?: string }[];\n  changes: FileChangePlan[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Deterministically validate and normalize a raw model plan. Malformed shapes\n * are reported as structured errors instead of throwing deep in the mapper, so\n * a single bad field cannot silently corrupt the report.\n */\nexport function validateModelPlanShape(raw: unknown): ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  const empty: ModelPlanShapeCheck = { ok: true, requirements: [], changes: [] };\n  if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan was not a JSON object.' };\n  }\n  const plan = raw as Record<string, unknown>;\n\n  if (plan.requirements !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.requirements)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"requirements\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n  if (plan.changes !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.changes)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"changes\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n\n  const requirements = (plan.requirements ?? []).map((req, index) => {\n    const item = (req ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id ? item.id : `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n      description: typeof item.description === 'string' ? item.description : '',\n      acceptanceCriteria: typeof item.acceptanceCriteria === 'string' ? item.acceptanceCriteria : '',\n      checkCommands: Array.isArray(item.checkCommands)\n        ? item.checkCommands.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && c.trim().length > 0)\n        : undefined,\n      manualReviewNote: typeof item.manualReviewNote === 'string' ? item.manualReviewNote : undefined,\n    };\n  });\n\n  const changes: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n  for (const change of (plan.changes ?? []) as unknown[]) {\n    const item = (change ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (typeof item.path !== 'string' || item.path.length === 0) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'A change is missing a \"path\".' };\n    }\n    if (!['create', 'modify', 'delete'].includes(String(item.action))) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has an invalid action \"${String(item.action)}\".` };\n    }\n    if (item.edits !== undefined && !Array.isArray(item.edits)) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has non-array edits.` };\n    }\n    changes.push({\n      path: item.path,\n      action: item.action as FileChangePlan['action'],\n      rationale: typeof item.rationale === 'string' ? item.rationale : '',\n      content: typeof item.content === 'string' ? item.content : undefined,\n      edits: Array.isArray(item.edits)\n        ? (item.edits as { find: string; replace: string }[])\n        : undefined,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, requirements, changes };\n}\n\n// Requested branch wins only when it is explicit and not the default; invalid\n// branches are resolved later (and fail closed) by the caller.\nexport function resolveTargetBranch(requested: string | undefined, defaultBranch: string): string {\n  const trimmed = requested?.trim();\n  return trimmed && trimmed !== defaultBranch ? trimmed : defaultBranch;\n}\n\n// A requirement is only PASS when a check named in its own acceptance criteria,\n// description, or explicit checkCommands actually passed. Unrelated green checks\n// cannot satisfy it, and a named-but-failing check yields FAIL, never PASS.\nexport function evaluateRequirementEvidence(\n  requirement: RequirementEvidenceInput,\n  results: { command: string; status: string; exitCode: number }[]\n): { status: 'PASS' | 'PENDING' | 'FAIL'; evidence: string } {\n  const attemptEvidence = results.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ');\n  const criterion = `${requirement.acceptanceCriteria ?? ''} ${requirement.description ?? []).map((c) => c.toLowerCase());\n  const referencedChecks = results.filter((result) => {\n    const lower = result.command.toLowerCase();\n    return explicit.includes(lower) || matchesCommand(result.command);\n  });\n\n  const failed = referencedChecks.filter((result) => result.status !== 'PASSED');\n  if (failed.length > 0) {\n    return {\n      status: 'FAIL',\n      evidence: `Criterion-named check failed: ${failed.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ')}.`,\n    };\n  }\n  if (referencedChecks.length > 0) {\n    return {\n      status: 'PASS',\n      evidence: `Criterion-matched checks passed: ${referencedChecks.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ')}.`,\n    };\n  }\n  const manual = requirement.manualReviewNote ? ` Manual review: ${requirement.manualReviewNote}.` : ' Manual review required.';\n  return {\n    status: 'PENDING',\n    evidence: `No criterion-specific passing check was identified. Latest target-check attempt: ${attemptEvidence}.${manual}`,\n  };\n}\n\nexport class ForgeAgent {\n  private github: GitHubService;\n  private model: ModelService;\n  private testRunner: TestRunnerService;\n  private githubToken?: string;\n\n  constructor(githubToken?: string) {\n    this.githubToken = githubToken?.trim();\n    this.github = new GitHubService(githubToken);\n    this.model = new ModelService();\n    this.testRunner = new TestRunnerService();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Strict validation of generated patch paths and contents (Fixes AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n   */\n  private validatePatch(changes: FileChangePlan[]): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {\n    const limits = loadForgeLimits();\n    if (!Array.isArray(changes) || changes.length === 0) {\n      return { valid: false, error: 'Empty patch: No file changes proposed.' };\n    }\n    if (changes.length > limits.maxFilesPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured file ceiling: ${changes.length} > ${limits.maxFilesPerMission}.` };\n    }\n    const totalEdits = changes.reduce((sum, change) => sum + (Array.isArray(change.edits) ? change.edits.length : 0), 0);\n    if (totalEdits > limits.maxEditsPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured edit ceiling: ${totalEdits} > ${limits.maxEditsPerMission}.` };\n    }\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      // 1. Path format validation (must be relative, no traversal)\n      if (!change.path || typeof change.path !== 'string') {\n        return { valid: false, error: 'Malformed patch: Missing or non-string file path.' };\n      }\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      if (path.isAbsolute(change.path) || portablePath.startsWith('/') || normalizedPath === '..' || normalizedPath.startsWith('../') || normalizedPath.includes('/../')) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Security Boundary Violation: Directory traversal or absolute path detected: \"${change.path}\".` };\n      }\n\n      // 2. content: string }[]\n  ): string[] {\n    const sourceByPath = new Map(contextFiles.map((file) => [file.path, file.content]));\n    const problems: string[] = [];\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      if (change.action !== 'modify' || !Array.isArray(change.edits) || change.edits.length === 0) continue;\n      const source = sourceByPath.get(change.path);\n      if (typeof source !== 'string') {\n        problems.push(`${change.path}: source content was not supplied to validate the edit anchors.`);\n        continue;\n      }\n      const result = applyExactEdits(source, change.edits);\n      if (!result.ok) problems.push(`${change.path}: ${result.error}`);\n    }\n    return problems;\n  }\n\n\n  private async applyChangesToWorktree(worktree: string, changes: FileChangePlan[]): Promise<void> {\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      const absolutePath = path.resolve(worktree, normalizedPath);\n      if (!absolutePath.startsWith(worktree + path.sep)) {\n        throw new Error(`Patch path escaped the isolated worktree: ${change.path}`);\n      }\n      const worktreeRealPath = await fs.realpath(worktree);\n      const relativeParent = path.relative(worktree, path.dirname(absolutePath));\n      let checkedParent = worktreeRealPath;\n      for (const segment of relativeParent.split(path.sep).filter(Boolean)) {\n        checkedParent = path.join(checkedParent, segment);\n        let parentStat;\n        try { parentStat = await fs.lstat(checkedParent); } catch (err: any) {\n        if (err?.code !== 'ENOENT') throw err;\n      }\n      if (targetStat?.isSymbolicLink()) throw new Error(`BLOCKED: refusing to patch symlink: ${change.path}`);\n      if (targetStat) {\n        const targetRealPath = await fs.realpath(absolutePath);\n        if (targetRealPath !== worktreeRealPath && !targetRealPath.startsWith(worktreeRealPath + path.sep)) {\n          throw new Error(`BLOCKED: patch target resolves outside the worktree: ${change.path}`);\n        }\n      }\n      const exists = Boolean(targetStat);\n      if (change.action === 'create' && exists) throw new Error(`Patch marked existing file as create: ${change.path}`);\n      if (change.action === 'modify' && !exists) throw new Error(`Patch marked missing file as modify: ${change.path}`);\n      if (change.action === 'modify' && Array.isArray(change.edits) && change.edits.length > 0) {\n        const current = await fs.readFile(absolutePath, 'utf-8');\n        const applied = applyExactEdits(current, change.edits);\n        if (!applied.ok) throw new Error(`Exact edit rejected in ${change.path}: ${applied.error}`);\n        await fs.writeFile(absolutePath, applied.content, 'utf-8');\n        // The GitHub commit API receives the verified full file from the tested worktree.\n        change.content = applied.content;\n      } else {\n        await fs.writeFile(absolutePath, change.content as string, 'utf-8');\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  async executeTask(task: TaskDefinition): Promise<TaskExecutionReport> {\n    const report: TaskExecutionReport = {\n      taskId: task.id,\n      status: 'QUEUED',\n      startTime: new Date().toISOString(),\n      baseCommitSha: 'UNKNOWN',\n      modelInvoked: {\n        provider: process.env.FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY === 'true' ? READING PERSISTENT INSTRUCTIONS & TARGET CODE SCOPE\n      log('info', 'Checking for persistent instructions in AGENTS.md');\n      const agentsMdRemote = await this.github.fetchFile(owner, repo, 'AGENTS.md', targetBranch);\n      let instructionText = '';\n      if (agentsMdRemote) {\n        instructionText = agentsMdRemote.content;\n        log('info', 'Loaded remote AGENTS.md instructions.');\n      } else {\n        try {\n          instructionText = await fs.readFile(path.resolve(process.cwd(), 'AGENTS.md'), 'utf-8');\n          log('info', 'Loaded local AGENTS.md instructions.');\n        } catch {\n          instructionText = 'Standard engineering instructions: inspect before editing, keep changes minimal.';\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Read target repository file inventory\n      log('info', 'Gathering repository file inventory for grounding');\n      const repoFilePaths = await this.github.listRepositoryFiles(owner, repo, targetBranch);\n      log('info', `Found ${repoFilePaths.length} files in target repository tree.`);\n\n      // Read the target repository's package manifest and bounded real source files.\n      const packageJsonRemote = []).map((req, index) => {\n    const item = (req ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id ? item.id : `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n      description: typeof item.description === 'string' ? item.description : '',\n      acceptanceCriteria: typeof item.acceptanceCriteria === 'string' ? item.acceptanceCriteria : '',\n      checkCommands: Array.isArray(item.checkCommands)\n        ? item.checkCommands.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && c.trim().length > 0)\n        : undefined,\n      manualReviewNote: typeof item.manualReviewNote === 'string' ? item.manualReviewNote : undefined,\n    };\n  });\n\n  const changes: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n  for (const change of (plan.changes ?? []) as unknown[]) {\n    const item = (change ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (typeof item.path !== 'string' || item.path.length === 0) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'A change is missing a \"path\".' };\n    }\n    if (!['create', 'modify', 'delete'].includes(String(item.action))) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has an invalid action \"${String(item.action)}\".` };\n    }\n    if (item.edits !== undefined && !Array.isArray(item.edits)) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has non-array edits.` };\n    }\n    changes.push({\n      path: item.path,\n      action: item.action as FileChangePlan['action'],\n      rationale: typeof item.rationale === 'string' ? item.rationale : '',\n      content: typeof item.content === 'string' ? item.content : undefined,\n      edits: Array.isArray(item.edits)\n        ? Latest target-check attempt: ${attemptEvidence}.${manual}`,\n  };\n}\n\nexport class ForgeAgent {\n  private github: GitHubService;\n  private model: ModelService;\n  private testRunner: TestRunnerService;\n  private githubToken?: string;\n\n  constructor(githubToken?: string) {\n    this.githubToken = githubToken?.trim();\n    this.github = new GitHubService(githubToken);\n    this.model = new ModelService();\n    this.testRunner = new TestRunnerService();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Strict validation of generated patch paths and contents (Fixes AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n   */\n  private validatePatch(changes: FileChangePlan[]): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {\n    const limits = loadForgeLimits();\n    if (!Array.isArray(changes) || changes.length === 0) {\n      return { valid: false, error: 'Empty patch: No file changes proposed.' };\n    }\n    if (changes.length > limits.maxFilesPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured file ceiling: ${changes.length} > ${limits.maxFilesPerMission}.` };\n    }\n    const totalEdits = changes.reduce((sum, change) => sum + (Array.isArray(change.edits) ? change.edits.length : 0), 0);\n    if (totalEdits > limits.maxEditsPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured edit ceiling: ${totalEdits} > ${limits.maxEditsPerMission}.` };\n    }\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      // 1.  "new_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport { TaskDefinition, TaskExecutionReport, FileChangePlan, RequirementEvidenceInput } from '../types/agent.ts';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { loadForgeLimits } from './limits.ts';\nimport { evaluatePermissionPolicy, loadPermissionConfig } from './policy.ts';\nimport { traceEntry } from './mission-trace.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport * as fs from 'fs/promises';\nimport * as path from 'path';\nimport * as os from 'os';\nimport { execFile } from 'child_process';\nimport { promisify } from 'util';\n\nconst execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);\n\n// Sensitive / Protected repository paths that Forge is prohibited from altering\nconst PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS = [\n  /^\\.git\\//i,\n  /^\\.env/i,\n  /^\\.github\\//i,\n  /^node_modules\\//i,\n  // Files executed by target checks must not be model-editable.\n  /(^|\\/)package(-lock)?\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)npm-shrinkwrap\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)\\.npmrc$/i,\n  /^vite\\.config\\.[cm]?[jt]s$/i,\n  /^tsconfig[^/]*\\.json$/i,\n  /^scripts\\//i,\n];\n\n// Keep the total source context bounded for anonymous models with small context windows.\nconst MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS = 24000;\n\n// Anonymous models sometimes wrap otherwise valid JSON in Markdown fences.\n// Normalize only that wrapper; JSON.parse remains the strict structural validator.\nfunction parseModelJson(text: string): any {\n  let normalized = text.trim();\n  if (normalized.startsWith('```')) {\n    const firstLineEnd = normalized.indexOf('\\n');\n    if (firstLineEnd >= 0) normalized = normalized.slice(firstLineEnd + 1);\n    const trimmedEnd = normalized.trimEnd();\n    if (trimmedEnd.endsWith('```')) normalized = trimmedEnd.slice(0, -3);\n    normalized = normalized.trim();\n  }\n  return JSON.parse(normalized);\n}\n\n// --- R6 resilience primitives -------------------------------------------------\n\nexport type FailureClass = 'RETRYABLE' | 'FATAL';\n\n/**\n * Classify a runtime failure so callers can retry transient conditions and stop\n * on permanent ones. Deterministic and pure so it is unit-testable.\n */\nexport function classifyFailure(error: unknown): FailureClass {\n  const message = (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)).toLowerCase();\n  const status = (error as { status?: number })?.status;\n  if (status === 429 || status === 408 || (typeof status === 'number' && status >= 500)) return 'RETRYABLE';\n  if (/abort|timeout|timed out|econnreset|enotfound|socket hang up|fetch failed|rate limit|429|5\\d\\d/.test(message)) {\n    return 'RETRYABLE';\n  }\n  return 'FATAL';\n}\n\nexport interface BoundedRetryOptions {\n  attempts: number;\n  baseDelayMs?: number;\n  maxDelayMs?: number;\n  /** Injected sleep so tests never wait on wall-clock time. */\n  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  isRetryable?: (error: unknown) => boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run an async operation with bounded retries and exponential backoff. Never\n * loops unbounded, never retries a fatal classification, and reports the exact\n * number of attempts so the caller can log truthful evidence.\n */\nexport async function withBoundedRetry<T>(\n  operation: () => Promise<T>,\n  options: BoundedRetryOptions\n): Promise<{ ok: true; value: T; attempts: number } | { ok: false; error: unknown; attempts: number }> {\n  const attempts = Math.max(1, Math.floor(options.attempts));\n  const base = options.baseDelayMs ?? 250;\n  const max = options.maxDelayMs ?? 2000;\n  const sleep = options.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms)));\n  const retryable = options.isRetryable ?? ((error: unknown) => classifyFailure(error) === 'RETRYABLE');\n\n  let lastError: unknown;\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {\n    try {\n      return { ok: true, value: await operation(), attempts: attempt };\n    } catch (error) {\n      lastError = error;\n      if (attempt >= attempts || !retryable(error)) {\n        return { ok: false, error, attempts: attempt };\n      }\n      const delay = Math.min(max, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1));\n      await sleep(delay);\n    }\n  }\n  return { ok: false, error: lastError, attempts };\n}\n\nexport interface ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  ok: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  requirements: { id: string; description: string; acceptanceCriteria: string; checkCommands?: string[]; manualReviewNote?: string }[];\n  changes: FileChangePlan[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Deterministically validate and normalize a raw model plan. Malformed shapes\n * are reported as structured errors instead of throwing deep in the mapper, so\n * a single bad field cannot silently corrupt the report.\n */\nexport function validateModelPlanShape(raw: unknown): ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  const empty: ModelPlanShapeCheck = { ok: true, requirements: [], changes: [] };\n  if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan was not a JSON object.' };\n  }\n  const plan = raw as Record<string, unknown>;\n\n  if (plan.requirements !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.requirements)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"requirements\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n  if (plan.changes !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.changes)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"changes\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n\n  const requirements = (plan.requirements ?? []).map((req, index) => {\n    const item = (req ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id ? item.id : `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n      description: typeof item.description === 'string' ? item.description : '',\n      acceptanceCriteria: typeof item.acceptanceCriteria === 'string' ? item.acceptanceCriteria : '',\n      checkCommands: Array.isArray(item.checkCommands)\n        ? item.checkCommands.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && c.trim().length > 0)\n        : undefined,\n      manualReviewNote: typeof item.manualReviewNote === 'string' ? item.manualReviewNote : undefined,\n    };\n  });\n\n  const changes: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n  for (const change of (plan.changes ?? []) as unknown[]) {\n    const item = (change ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (typeof item.path !== 'string' || item.path.length === 0) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'A change is missing a \"path\".' };\n    }\n    if (!['create', 'modify', 'delete'].includes(String(item.action))) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has an invalid action \"${String(item.action)}\".` };\n    }\n    if (item.edits !== undefined && !Array.isArray(item.edits)) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has non-array edits.` };\n    }\n    changes.push({\n      path: item.path,\n      action: item.action as FileChangePlan['action'],\n      rationale: typeof item.rationale === 'string' ? item.rationale : '',\n      content: typeof item.content === 'string' ? item.content : undefined,\n      edits: Array.isArray(item.edits)\n        ? (item.edits as { find: string; replace: string }[])\n        : undefined,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, requirements, changes };\n}\n\n// Requested branch wins only when it is explicit and not the default; invalid\n// branches are resolved later (and fail closed) by the caller.\nexport function resolveTargetBranch(requested: string | undefined, defaultBranch: string): string {\n  const trimmed = requested?.trim();\n  return trimmed && trimmed !== defaultBranch ? trimmed : defaultBranch;\n}\n\n// A requirement is only PASS when a check named in its own acceptance criteria,\n// description, or explicit checkCommands actually passed. Unrelated green checks\n// cannot satisfy it, and a named-but-failing check yields FAIL, never PASS.\nexport function evaluateRequirementEvidence(\n  requirement: RequirementEvidenceInput,\n  results: { command: string; status: string; exitCode: number }[]\n): { status: 'PASS' | 'PENDING' | 'FAIL'; evidence: string } {\n  const attemptEvidence = results.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ');\n  const criterion = `${requirement.acceptanceCriteria ?? ''} ${requirement.description ?? ''}`.toLowerCase();\n\n  const matchesCommand = (command: string): boolean => {\n    const lower = command.toLowerCase();\n    const scriptName = lower === 'npm test' ?  "new_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport { TaskDefinition, TaskExecutionReport, FileChangePlan, RequirementEvidenceInput } from '../types/agent.ts';\nimport { GitHubService } from '../services/github.ts';\nimport { ModelService } from '../services/model.ts';\nimport { TestRunnerService } from '../services/test-runner.ts';\nimport { loadForgeLimits } from './limits.ts';\nimport { evaluatePermissionPolicy, loadPermissionConfig } from './policy.ts';\nimport { traceEntry } from './mission-trace.ts';\nimport { applyExactEdits } from './stages.ts';\nimport * as fs from 'fs/promises';\nimport * as path from 'path';\nimport * as os from 'os';\nimport { execFile } from 'child_process';\nimport { promisify } from 'util';\n\nconst execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);\n\n// Sensitive / Protected repository paths that Forge is prohibited from altering\nconst PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS = [\n  /^\\.git\\//i,\n  /^\\.env/i,\n  /^\\.github\\//i,\n  /^node_modules\\//i,\n  // Files executed by target checks must not be model-editable.\n  /(^|\\/)package(-lock)?\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)npm-shrinkwrap\\.json$/i,\n  /(^|\\/)\\.npmrc$/i,\n  /^vite\\.config\\.[cm]?[jt]s$/i,\n  /^tsconfig[^/]*\\.json$/i,\n  /^scripts\\//i,\n];\n\n// Keep the total source context bounded for anonymous models with small context windows.\nconst MAX_SOURCE_CONTEXT_CHARS = 24000;\n\n// Anonymous models sometimes wrap otherwise valid JSON in Markdown fences.\n// Normalize only that wrapper; JSON.parse remains the strict structural validator.\nfunction parseModelJson(text: string): any {\n  let normalized = text.trim();\n  if (normalized.startsWith('```')) {\n    const firstLineEnd = normalized.indexOf('\\n');\n    if (firstLineEnd >= 0) normalized = normalized.slice(firstLineEnd + 1);\n    const trimmedEnd = normalized.trimEnd();\n    if (trimmedEnd.endsWith('```')) normalized = trimmedEnd.slice(0, -3);\n    normalized = normalized.trim();\n  }\n  return JSON.parse(normalized);\n}\n\n// --- R6 resilience primitives -------------------------------------------------\n\nexport type FailureClass = 'RETRYABLE' | 'FATAL';\n\n/**\n * Classify a runtime failure so callers can retry transient conditions and stop\n * on permanent ones. Deterministic and pure so it is unit-testable.\n */\nexport function classifyFailure(error: unknown): FailureClass {\n  const message = (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)).toLowerCase();\n  const status = (error as { status?: number })?.status;\n  if (status === 429 || status === 408 || (typeof status === 'number' && status >= 500)) return 'RETRYABLE';\n  if (/abort|timeout|timed out|econnreset|enotfound|socket hang up|fetch failed|rate limit|429|5\\d\\d/.test(message)) {\n    return 'RETRYABLE';\n  }\n  return 'FATAL';\n}\n\nexport interface BoundedRetryOptions {\n  attempts: number;\n  baseDelayMs?: number;\n  maxDelayMs?: number;\n  /** Injected sleep so tests never wait on wall-clock time. */\n  sleep?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  isRetryable?: (error: unknown) => boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * Run an async operation with bounded retries and exponential backoff. Never\n * loops unbounded, never retries a fatal classification, and reports the exact\n * number of attempts so the caller can log truthful evidence.\n */\nexport async function withBoundedRetry<T>(\n  operation: () => Promise<T>,\n  options: BoundedRetryOptions\n): Promise<{ ok: true; value: T; attempts: number } | { ok: false; error: unknown; attempts: number }> {\n  const attempts = Math.max(1, Math.floor(options.attempts));\n  const base = options.baseDelayMs ?? 250;\n  const max = options.maxDelayMs ?? 2000;\n  const sleep = options.sleep ?? ((ms: number) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms)));\n  const retryable = options.isRetryable ?? ((error: unknown) => classifyFailure(error) === 'RETRYABLE');\n\n  let lastError: unknown;\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {\n    try {\n      return { ok: true, value: await operation(), attempts: attempt };\n    } catch (error) {\n      lastError = error;\n      if (attempt >= attempts || !retryable(error)) {\n        return { ok: false, error, attempts: attempt };\n      }\n      const delay = Math.min(max, base * 2 ** (attempt - 1));\n      await sleep(delay);\n    }\n  }\n  return { ok: false, error: lastError, attempts };\n}\n\nexport interface ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  ok: boolean;\n  error?: string;\n  requirements: { id: string; description: string; acceptanceCriteria: string; checkCommands?: string[]; manualReviewNote?: string }[];\n  changes: FileChangePlan[];\n}\n\n/**\n * Deterministically validate and normalize a raw model plan. Malformed shapes\n * are reported as structured errors instead of throwing deep in the mapper, so\n * a single bad field cannot silently corrupt the report.\n */\nexport function validateModelPlanShape(raw: unknown): ModelPlanShapeCheck {\n  const empty: ModelPlanShapeCheck = { ok: true, requirements: [], changes: [] };\n  if (!raw || typeof raw !== 'object') {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan was not a JSON object.' };\n  }\n  const plan = raw as Record<string, unknown>;\n\n  if (plan.requirements !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.requirements)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"requirements\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n  if (plan.changes !== undefined && !Array.isArray(plan.changes)) {\n    return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'Model plan \"changes\" must be an array when present.' };\n  }\n\n  const requirements = (plan.requirements ?? []).map((req, index) => {\n    const item = (req ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      id: typeof item.id === 'string' && item.id ? item.id : `REQ-${index + 1}`,\n      description: typeof item.description === 'string' ? item.description : '',\n      acceptanceCriteria: typeof item.acceptanceCriteria === 'string' ? item.acceptanceCriteria : '',\n      checkCommands: Array.isArray(item.checkCommands)\n        ? item.checkCommands.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string' && c.trim().length > 0)\n        : undefined,\n      manualReviewNote: typeof item.manualReviewNote === 'string' ? item.manualReviewNote : undefined,\n    };\n  });\n\n  const changes: FileChangePlan[] = [];\n  for (const change of (plan.changes ?? []) as unknown[]) {\n    const item = (change ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    if (typeof item.path !== 'string' || item.path.length === 0) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: 'A change is missing a \"path\".' };\n    }\n    if (!['create', 'modify', 'delete'].includes(String(item.action))) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has an invalid action \"${String(item.action)}\".` };\n    }\n    if (item.edits !== undefined && !Array.isArray(item.edits)) {\n      return { ...empty, ok: false, error: `Change \"${item.path}\" has non-array edits.` };\n    }\n    changes.push({\n      path: item.path,\n      action: item.action as FileChangePlan['action'],\n      rationale: typeof item.rationale === 'string' ? item.rationale : '',\n      content: typeof item.content === 'string' ? item.content : undefined,\n      edits: Array.isArray(item.edits)\n        ? (item.edits as { find: string; replace: string }[])\n        : undefined,\n    });\n  }\n\n  return { ok: true, requirements, changes };\n}\n\n// Requested branch wins only when it is explicit and not the default; invalid\n// branches are resolved later (and fail closed) by the caller.\nexport function resolveTargetBranch(requested: string | undefined, defaultBranch: string): string {\n  const trimmed = requested?.trim();\n  return trimmed && trimmed !== defaultBranch ? trimmed : defaultBranch;\n}\n\n// A requirement is only PASS when a check named in its own acceptance criteria,\n// description, or explicit checkCommands actually passed. Unrelated green checks\n// cannot satisfy it, and a named-but-failing check yields FAIL, never PASS.\nexport function evaluateRequirementEvidence(\n  requirement: RequirementEvidenceInput,\n  results: { command: string; status: string; exitCode: number }[]\n): { status: 'PASS' | 'PENDING' | 'FAIL'; evidence: string } {\n  const attemptEvidence = results.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ');\n  const criterion = `${requirement.acceptanceCriteria ?? ''} ${requirement.description ?? []).map((c) => c.toLowerCase());\n  const referencedChecks = results.filter((result) => {\n    const lower = result.command.toLowerCase();\n    return explicit.includes(lower) || matchesCommand(result.command);\n  });\n\n  const failed = referencedChecks.filter((result) => result.status !== 'PASSED');\n  if (failed.length > 0) {\n    return {\n      status: 'FAIL',\n      evidence: `Criterion-named check failed: ${failed.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ')}.`,\n    };\n  }\n  if (referencedChecks.length > 0) {\n    return {\n      status: 'PASS',\n      evidence: `Criterion-matched checks passed: ${referencedChecks.map((result) => `${result.command}=${result.exitCode}`).join(', ')}.`,\n    };\n  }\n  const manual = requirement.manualReviewNote ? ` Manual review: ${requirement.manualReviewNote}.` : ' Manual review required.';\n  return {\n    status: 'PENDING',\n    evidence: `No criterion-specific passing check was identified. Latest target-check attempt: ${attemptEvidence}.${manual}`,\n  };\n}\n\nexport class ForgeAgent {\n  private github: GitHubService;\n  private model: ModelService;\n  private testRunner: TestRunnerService;\n  private githubToken?: string;\n\n  constructor(githubToken?: string) {\n    this.githubToken = githubToken?.trim();\n    this.github = new GitHubService(githubToken);\n    this.model = new ModelService();\n    this.testRunner = new TestRunnerService();\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Strict validation of generated patch paths and contents (Fixes AUD-20261012-02 Patch Validation)\n   */\n  private validatePatch(changes: FileChangePlan[]): { valid: boolean; error?: string } {\n    const limits = loadForgeLimits();\n    if (!Array.isArray(changes) || changes.length === 0) {\n      return { valid: false, error: 'Empty patch: No file changes proposed.' };\n    }\n    if (changes.length > limits.maxFilesPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured file ceiling: ${changes.length} > ${limits.maxFilesPerMission}.` };\n    }\n    const totalEdits = changes.reduce((sum, change) => sum + (Array.isArray(change.edits) ? change.edits.length : 0), 0);\n    if (totalEdits > limits.maxEditsPerMission) {\n      return { valid: false, error: `Patch exceeds the configured edit ceiling: ${totalEdits} > ${limits.maxEditsPerMission}.` };\n    }\n\n    for (const change of changes) {\n      // 1. Path format validation (must be relative, no traversal)\n      if (!change.path || typeof change.path !== 'string') {\n        return { valid: false, error: 'Malformed patch: Missing or non-string file path.' };\n      }\n      const portablePath = change.path.replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n      const normalizedPath = path.posix.normalize(portablePath).replace(/^(\\.\\/)+/, '');\n      if (path.isAbsolute(change.path) || portablePath.startsWith('/') || normalizedPath === '..' || normalizedPath.startsWith('../') || normalizedPath.includes('/../')) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Security Boundary Violation: Directory traversal or absolute path detected: \"${change.path}\".` };\n      }\n\n      // 2. Protected files check\n      if (PROTECTED_PATH_PATTERNS.some((pat) => pat.test(normalizedPath))) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Security Boundary Violation: Modification of protected file or path is forbidden: \"${change.path}\".` };\n      }\n      change.path = normalizedPath; // commit exactly the path that was tested\n\n      // 3. Action and content check\n      if (!['modify', 'create'].includes(change.action)) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Unsupported or dangerous patch action \"${change.action}\". Only create and modify are supported.` };\n      }\n      const hasContent = typeof change.content === 'string' && change.content.length > 0;\n      const hasEdits = Array.isArray(change.edits) && change.edits.length > 0\n        && change.edits.every((edit) => edit && typeof edit.find === 'string' && edit.find.length > 0 && typeof edit.replace === 'string');\n      if ((change.action === 'create' && !hasContent) || (change.action === 'modify' && !hasContent && !hasEdits)) {\n        return { valid: false, error: `Invalid patch: \"${change.path}\" needs complete content for create or valid exact edits for modify.` };\n      }\n      const patchSize = hasContent ?
