Excellent! Now I see it. The implementer:
1. read_file index.js ✓
2. write_file → FAILED "File exists. Use edit_file."
3. edit_file → ok ✓ (the file WAS changed on disk)
4. run_check test → PASSED ✓
5. finish ✓

**The file was actually changed on disk** (`index.js now: module.exports = { version: '1.0.0' };`), and the test PASSED. But `changes: []` — the change map is EMPTY!

Why? Look at team.ts capture:
```js
for (const step of loop.steps) {
  if (step.action.tool !== 'write_file' || !step.observation.ok) continue;
  const rel = step.action.input?.path;
  ...
  changes[rel] = readFileSync(...)
}
```

It only captures **`write_file`** steps that succeeded! It does NOT capture **`edit_file`** steps. The implementer used `edit_file` (because `write_file` refuses to overwrite existing files — a deliberate safety feature). So the real edit is invisible to the change map → `integrate` sees zero changes → "no change produced" → BLOCKED.

**This is the concrete defect: `runTeam` records changes from `write_file` only, ignoring `edit_file`.** Since the prompt explicitly instructs "To change an existing file, use edit_file", the primary way a role edits an existing file is never captured. So the company can never report a change when the implementer edits an existing file — which is the normal case. This is exactly "the ability to get the job done correctly the first time" failing.

The fix: in team.ts, also capture `edit_file` steps (and ideally any mutating tool that reports a path). Minimal fix: treat `edit_file` like `write_file` in the capture loop.

Let me confirm: the loop capture is at team.ts lines ~108-118. Change:
```js
if (step.action.tool !== 'write_file' || !step.observation.ok) continue;
```
to
```js
const MUTATING = new Set(['write_file', 'edit_file']);
if (!MUTATING.has(step.action.tool) || !step.observation.ok) continue;
```

That's the minimal, correct fix. Let me also check if there are other mutating tools (e.g., a delete). Let me grep role-tools.ts for tool names.

Also note: the `changes` map should reflect the FINAL file content (read from disk), which the code does via readFileSync — good.

Let me check role-tools.ts for all mutating tools.

Every write is recorded so the team's change map reflects disk.\n */\nimport { buildWorkspaceTools, type AgentTool } from '../kernel/loop.ts';\nimport { runCommand } from './runner.ts';\n\nexport interface RoleToolsOptions {\n  /** The real directory this role works in. */\n  workspaceDir: string;\n  /** True for `branch-write` roles. */\n  canMutate: boolean;\n  /** Relative path prefixes a write is confined to. Defaults to the whole workspace. */\n  allowedRoots?: string[];\n  /** Authorized verification commands: label -> command. */\n  authorizedCommands?: Record<string, string>;\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_COMMANDS: Record<string, string> = {\n  test: 'npm test',\n  lint: 'npm run lint',\n};\n\nexport function buildRoleTools(options: RoleToolsOptions): AgentTool[] {\n  const roots = options.allowedRoots?.length ? options.allowedRoots : [''];\n  const authorized = options.authorizedCommands ?? DEFAULT_COMMANDS;\n\n  const base = buildWorkspaceTools({\n    workspace: options.workspaceDir,\n    allowMutation: options.canMutate,\n    authorizedCommands: authorized,\n    runner: (command, cwd) => runCommand(command, cwd),\n  });\n\n  return base.map((tool) => {\n    if (tool.name !== 'write_file' && tool.name !== 'edit_file') return tool;\n    const original = tool.run;\n    return {\n      ...tool,\n      run: async (input, ctx) => {\n        const rel = typeof input.path === 'string' ? input.path : '';\n        if (!roots.some((root) => root === '' || rel === root || rel.startsWith(root.endsWith('/') ? root : root + '/'))) {\n          return { ok: false, output: `Refusing to write outside the allowed roots (${roots.join(', ')}): ${rel}` };\n        }\n        return original(input, ctx);\n      },\n    };\n  });\n}"

'check'), status: s.observation.ok ? 'PASSED' : 'FAILED' }));\n      if (observed.length) result.data = { ...result.data, checks: observed };\n    }\n\n    // A mutating role records the files it changed. `files` must be a path->content\n    // map; a plain list of touched names (e.g. from a design) is not a change.\n    const wrote = result.data.files;\n    if (wrote && typeof wrote === 'object' && !Array.isArray(wrote)) {\n      Object.assign(changes, wrote as Record<string, string>);\n    }\n    // Capture files the role actually wrote to disk, so the change map reflects\n    // real writes even when the brain did not enumerate them in its finish data.\n    // `edit_file` is included: the role prompt requires it for existing files\n    // (write_file is refused on an existing path), so an edit-only role would\n    // otherwise report no change and the company would block a real success.\n    if (options.workspaceDir) {\n      for (const step of loop.steps) {\n        if (!MUTATING_TOOLS.has(step.action.tool) || !step.observation.ok) continue;\n        const rel = step.action.input?.path;\n        if (typeof rel !== 'string') continue;\n        try {\n          changes[rel] = readFileSync(path.join(options.workspaceDir, rel), 'utf8');\n        } catch {\n          /* file vanished; skip */\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    bus.post({ kind: role.produces, author: role.id, scope, summary: result.summary, data: { ...result.data, changes: { ...changes } } });\n    results.push({ role: role.id, result });\n\n    if (!result.ok && stopOnFailure) {\n      return { workItem, status: 'BLOCKED', reason: `${role.id} failed: ${result.reason ?? result.summary}`, results, changes };\n    }\n  }\n\n  const failed = results.some((r) => !r.result.ok);\n  return {\n    workItem,\n    status: failed ? 'ok' : 'FAILED'}: ${h.observation.output.slice(0, 4000)}`).join('\\n')\n    : '(no actions yet)';\n  const upstream = state.memory?.trim() ? `What earlier roles produced (JSON, oldest first):\\n${state.memory.trim().slice(0, 6000)}\\n` : '';\n  const sequence = spec.sequence?.length\n    ? `Required sequence for your role (follow it in order, one action per reply):\\n${spec.sequence.map((s, i) => `  ${i + 1}. ${s}`).join('\\n')}\\n`\n    : '';\n  return `You are the ${spec.role} in a software company. list)'],\n  qa: ['run_check the \"test\" command', 'run_check the \"lint\" command', 'finish with your evidence artifact'],\n  security: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your security artifact (data.clean = boolean, data.findings = list)'],\n  release: ['finish with your decision artifact (data.ship = boolean)'],\n};\n\n/**\n * Work tier per role. Easy work — turning a goal into requirements, reviewing a\n * diff, recording evidence, deciding to ship — needs no provider key, so it rides\n * the free keyless routes. 'easy' : 'hard';\n}\n\nfunction modelRoster(model: ModelService, attempt: number, workspaceDir: string): Role[] {\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({\n      workspaceDir,\n      canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write',\n      allowedRoots: [''],\n      authorizedCommands: TARGET_COMMANDS,\n    }),\n    brain: modelBrain(model, {\n      role: `${r.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      sequence: ROLE_SEQUENCE[r.id],\n      artifactHint: `Emit your \"${r.produces}\" artifact in data.`,\n      tier: tierForRole(r.id),\n    }),\n  }));\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const args = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const useModel = args.includes('--model');\n  const wsIdx = args.indexOf('--workspace');\n  const explicitTarget = wsIdx >= 0 ? args[wsIdx + 1] : undefined;\n  const useTarget = args.includes('--target') || Boolean(explicitTarget);\n  const goal = args.filter((a, i) => a !== '--model' && a !== '--target' && a !== '--workspace' && !(wsIdx >= 0 && i === wsIdx + 1)).join(' ').trim() || 'Demonstrate the company on a sample goal.';\n\n  const workspaceDir = useTarget ? explicitTarget ?? sampleTarget() : undefined;\n  if (workspaceDir) console.log(`[target] ${workspaceDir}${explicitTarget ? {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction scriptedBrain(id: string, attempt: number): AgentBrain {\n  const script: AgentAction[] = [\n    { tool: 'think', input: { thought: `${id} plans the work` } },\n    { tool: scriptedRoster(attempt: number): Role[] {\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: [{ name: 'think', description: 'noop', run: async () => ({ ok: true, output: 'ok' }) }],\n    brain: scriptedBrain(r.id, attempt),\n  }));\n}\n\n/** An explicit file', 'write_file with the new content', 'run_check the \"test\" command', 'finish with your change artifact (data.summary)'],\n  reviewer: ['read_file on the changed file', 'finish with your review artifact (data.blockers = number, data.notes = list)'],\n  qa: ['run_check the \"test\" command', 'run_check the \"lint\" command', 'finish with your evidence artifact'],\n  security: ['read_file on tier per role. Easy work — turning a goal into requirements, reviewing a\n * diff, recording evidence, deciding to ship — needs no provider key, so it rides\n * the free keyless routes. 'easy' : 'hard';\n}\n\nfunction modelRoster(model: ModelService, attempt: number, workspaceDir: string): Role[] {\n  return DEFAULT_ROSTER.map((r) => ({\n    id: r.id,\n    title: r.title,\n    mandate: r.mandate,\n    authority: r.authority,\n    consumes: r.consumes,\n    produces: r.produces,\n    tools: buildRoleTools({\n      workspaceDir,\n      canMutate: r.authority === 'branch-write',\n      allowedRoots: [''],\n      authorizedCommands: TARGET_COMMANDS,\n    }),\n    brain: modelBrain(model, {\n      role: `${r.title} (attempt ${attempt})`,\n      mandate: r.mandate,\n      sequence: ROLE_SEQUENCE[r.id],\n      artifactHint: `Emit your \"${r.produces}\" artifact in data.`,\n      tier: tierForRole(r.id),\n    }),\n  }));\n}\n\nasync function main(): Promise<void> {\n  const args = process.argv.slice(2);\n  const useModel = args.includes('--model');\n  const wsIdx = args.indexOf('--workspace');\n  const explicitTarget = wsIdx >= 0 ? args[wsIdx + 1] : undefined;\n  const useTarget = args.includes('--target') || Boolean(explicitTarget);\n  const goal = args.filter((a, i) => a !== '--model' && a !== '--target' && a !== '--workspace' && !(wsIdx >= 0 && i === wsIdx + 1)).join(' ').trim() || 'Demonstrate the company on a sample goal.';\n\n  const workspaceDir = useTarget ? explicitTarget ?? sampleTarget() : undefined;\n  if (workspaceDir) console.log(`[target] ${workspaceDir}${explicitTarget ? Object.keys(result.integratedChanges).join(', ') : '(none)');\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

'' : ' (generated sample)'}`);\n\n  const bus = new ArtifactBus();\n  const model = useModel ? new ModelService() : null;\n  if (model) {\n    const info = model.getProviderInfo();\n    console.log(`[model] ${info.primaryProvider}; Gemini fallback configured: ${info.fallbackConfigured}`);\n  }\n\n  const attemptsPerItem = Math.max(1, Number.parseInt(process.env.FORGE_COMPANY_ATTEMPTS ?? '', 10) || 2);\n  const result = await runCompany({\n    goal,\n    bus,\n    plan: (g) => [{ id: 'w1', title: g }],\n    rosterFor: (_item, attempt) => (model ? modelRoster(model, attempt, workspaceDir ?? process.cwd()) : scriptedRoster(attempt)),\n    attemptsPerItem,\n    workspaceDir,\n    integrate: ({ changes }) => ({ ok: Object.keys(changes).length > 0, reason: Object.keys(changes).length ? `${Object.keys(changes).length} file(s) changed` : 'no change produced' }),\n  });\n\n  console.log('--- FORGE COMPANY REPORT ---');\n  console.log('Goal:', result.goal);\n  console.log('Status:', result.status);\n  console.log('Reason:', result.reason);\n  console.log('Winners:', result.winners.join(', ') || '(none)');\n  console.log('Artifacts:', bus.all().length);\n  for (const item of result.items) {\n    console.log(`- ${item.item.title}: ${item.competition.reason}`);\n    for (const card of item.competition.scorecards) {\n      console.log(`    ${card.attempt}: ${card.total} pt(s)${card.eligible ? '' : ' [ineligible]'}`);\n    }\n  }\n  console.log('Changed files:', Object.keys(result.integratedChanges).length ? Object.keys(result.integratedChanges).join(', ') : '(none)');\n  console.log('Routing: easy roles (pm, architect, reviewer, qa, security, release) ride keyless; implementer is hard (keys first).');\n  if (result.status !== 'COMPLETED') process.exitCode = 1;\n}\n\nmain().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('[forge-company] failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err));\n  process.exitCode = 1;\n});\n",

   "text": "############ docs/CHATGPT-OPERATING-FORGE.md ############\n# Operating Forge — A Manual for the Controller LLM (ChatGPT)\n\nThis document teaches a controller model (ChatGPT, Gemini, or any LLM with repository\naccess) how to **direct Forge correctly**. Read it before you open a Forge task, and read\nit again before you turn a Forge report into a change request. It is written to be\nfollowed literally.\n\nForge is not a chatbot you converse with. It is a **deterministic, bounded coding agent**\nthat you trigger, then read the evidence from. Treat it like a build system: you submit a\nwell-formed task, you wait, you read the report. You do not \"chat\" it into changing its mind.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What Forge is (and is not)\n\n**Forge is:**\n- A GitHub-Actions-hosted agent that takes a task, plans a bounded patch, applies it to an\n  **isolated branch**, runs the target checks, and opens a **pull request**.\n- Fully evidence-producing: every mission emits a machine-readable report and an artifact.\n- Conservative by design: it cannot push to `main`, cannot merge, and cannot act outside an\n  allow-list unless an operator widens its profile.\n\n**Forge is not:**\n- An interactive assistant. One task = one bounded mission.\n- A free-form \"do anything\" agent. It has hard ceilings (see §7).\n- Self-approving. A separate verifier (the **Sentinel**) decides whether its work may merge.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The mental model: a pipeline, not a loop\n\nA Forge mission moves through a **fixed stage sequence** (recorded in the mission trace):\n\n```\nVALIDATE → INSPECT → PLAN → APPLY → TEST → COMMIT → PR → POLICY\n```\n\nTrace stage names you will see: `INSPECT`, `PLAN`, `VALIDATE`, `APPLY`, `TEST`, `COMMIT`,\n`PR`, `POLICY`. Each stage has a status: `STARTED`, `PASSED`, `FAILED`, `BLOCKED`, `SKIPPED`.\n\nKey consequence: **Forge can self-repair inside a stage** (e.g. fix a failing test up to\n`maxRepairAttempts`), but it **cannot decide to do something outside the sequence**. If your\ntask needs open-ended exploration, Forge will not do it yet — that is the future \"loop\"\nmilestone, not today's behaviour. Write tasks that fit the pipeline.\n\n---\n\n## 3. How to trigger Forge\n\nThere are exactly **two** entry points. Pick one deliberately.\n\n### Path A — Open an issue and label it (preferred for coding)\n\n1. Create an issue in `madnessgate44-debug/Firstborn` whose **body is the task**.\n2. Add the label **`forge-task`**.\n3. The issue **must be authored by the repository owner** (`author_association == OWNER`),\n   or the workflow will not run.\n\nThe issue title becomes the task title; the issue body becomes the task description.\nForge's branch will be named `forge/task-<issue-number>-<run-id>`, and it will open a PR.\n\n### Path B — Dispatch the workflow (for a one-off or an audit)\n\nUse `Actions → Forge Coding Agent → Run workflow`. Inputs:\n\n| Input | Meaning | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| `mode` | `coding` or `audit` | `audit` runs the separate read-only job |\n| `target_repo` | `owner/repo` | **Required for audit mode** |\n| `task_id` | short identifier | becomes part of the branch name |\n| `task_title` | human title | |\n| `task_desc` | the task body | same rules as §4 |\n\n### Path C — Audit a repository (read-only)\n\nEither dispatch `mode=audit` with `target_repo=owner/repo`, or open an issue labeled\n**`forge-audit`** (owner-authored) with the repo URL in the body. The audit job:\n- reads only via GitHub's public API (no clone, no execution),\n- **cannot write anything** (job permissions are `contents: read`),\n- produces an inventory plus **model-backed findings** (architecture, gaps, prioritized\n  defects) that are **path-cited** and labelled `observed` vs `inferred`.\n\n---\n\n## 4. How to write a task that Forge can actually complete\n\nForge is bounded. A task it cannot fit returns valid JSON with **no changes** and an\nexplanation — that is a correct outcome, not a failure. Write tasks to avoid it.\n\n**Rules for a good task:**\n1. **State the goal in one sentence.**\n2. **Name the files** if you know them. Forge must not guess paths.\n3. **State the acceptance check** (\"`npm test` must pass\", \"`npm run lint` must be clean\").\n4. **Keep it small.** Defaults allow ~5 files and ~8 edits per mission. If you need more,\n   split it into several missions.\n5. **Say what must not change** (\"do not touch unrelated files\").\n6. **Do not embed instructions to Forge about its own behaviour** in repository content you\n   expect it to read; Forge treats repository content as untrusted data.\n\n**Good task body:**\n```\nGoal: Make the model health check forward every provider key.\n\nFiles: .github/workflows/model-health.yml\nAcceptance: the workflow forwards GROQ_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, and any FREELM_*_KEYS\nvariants; `npm run lint` passes; no other workflow is modified.\nDo not alter src/.\n```\n\n**Bad task body:**\n```\nImprove the whole repo and make it better, also fix anything you find.\n```\n(This has no bound, no files, and no acceptance check. Forge will refuse or do very little.)\n\n---\n\n## 5. How to read a Forge report\n\nThe report is written to `.firstborn/evidence/<task-id>.json` and uploaded as the\n**`forge-evidence`** artifact. Fields you must check, in order:\n\n| Field | What to look for |\n|---|---|\n| `status` | `SUCCESS` / `FAILED` / `BLOCKED` |\n| `baseCommitSha` | the exact commit Forge started from (record this) |\n| `branchName` | the isolated branch it wrote to |\n| `headCommitSha` | the commit it produced |\n| `prUrl` | the pull request, if opened |\n| `modelInvoked.provider` / `.model` | which model actually answered |\n| `requirements[]` | the numbered requirements + acceptance criteria it derived |\n| `testResults[]` | the checks it ran and their results |\n| `diagnosis` | on failure: `category`, `severity`, `summary`, `recovery`, `retryable` |\n| `trace[]` | the stage-by-stage record (`STARTED`/`PASSED`/`FAILED`/`BLOCKED`) |\n| `errorMessage` / `blockerReason` | why it stopped |\n\n**Golden rule: never trust a claim that is not in the report.** If the report does not show\na passing check, the check did not pass. If there is no `prUrl`, no PR exists.\n\n### Diagnosis categories (what a stop means)\n\n- **RETRYABLE** (e.g. model route 429/5xx): a re-run may succeed.\n- **FATAL / manual**: do not blindly re-run; the task or environment needs a change.\n- **BLOCKED** (policy): Forge was correctly denied a write. Do not \"fix\" this by loosening\n  policy unless a human decides to.\n\n---\n\n## 6. The safety model — what Forge may and may not do\n\nForge's authority comes from **`src/agent/policy.ts`**, which is the single control plane.\n\n| Profile | May branch | May commit | May open PR | May merge |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| `readonly` | no | no | no | no |\n| `sandbox` | yes | yes | no | no |\n| `review` (default) | yes | yes | yes | **no** |\n| `publish` | yes | yes | yes | **no** |\n\n**Merge is never granted by Forge.** That seat is reserved. A **separate** verifier — the\n**Sentinel** — owns the merge decision.\n\n### The Sentinel (the automated reviewer)\n\nWhen Forge opens a PR from a `forge/*` branch, the Sentinel workflow:\n1. re-runs the deterministic checks (`lint`, `build`, `test`) — these are the **authority**;\n2. optionally consults a model judge (off by default; can only add caution);\n3. merges **only if** all required checks passed **and** the operator has set the repository\n   variable `SENTINEL_AUTO_MERGE=true`.\n\nIf a required check did not run, it counts as **failed**. If the judge is uncertain, the\nSentinel **holds**. The Sentinel never treats Forge's own claim as evidence.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Hard limits (defaults you must design around)\n\nFrom `src/agent/limits.ts` (all overridable by environment, all bounded):\n\n| Limit | Default | Meaning |\n|---|---|---|\n| `maxFilesPerMission` | 5 | files a mission may touch |\n| `maxEditsPerMission` | 8 | edits per mission |\n| `maxPatchBytes` | 100 KB | total patch size |\n| `maxModelCalls` | 6 | model invocations |\n| `maxRepairAttempts` | 2 | self-repair rounds |\n| `maxRuntimeMs` | 10 min | wall-clock ceiling |\n| `maxMissionAttempts` | 1 | mission-level retries |\n\nCoding missions run **keyless/free** (`FIRSTBORN_KEYLESS_ONLY=true`); audits run **keyed**\n(hard work). Do not assume a coding mission has paid-model quality.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Operating recipes\n\n**Recipe 1 — ask Forge to fix something**\n1. Open an issue, owner-authored, body per §4.\n2. Label it `forge-task`.\n3. Wait for the run. Read the report (§5).\n4. If `status=SUCCESS` and a `prUrl` exists, hand the PR to the Sentinel (it runs\n   automatically). Do not merge it yourself.\n\n**Recipe 2 — audit a repository**\n1. Open an owner-authored issue with the repo URL in the body, label `forge-audit`.\n2. Wait. Read the artifact `forge-readonly-audit` (JSON + Markdown).\n3. **Verify before you act:** every finding cites a real path; treat `inferred` findings as\n   hypotheses, `observed` findings as evidenced.\n4. Only findings that cite real paths are safe to turn into change requests.\n\n**Recipe 3 — turn an audit into work**\n1. Take one finding.\n2. Write it as a bounded task (§4) with the cited path and an acceptance check.\n3. Open it as a `forge-task` issue.\n4. Do not bundle several findings into one task; split them.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Troubleshooting\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| Workflow did not start | issue not owner-authored, or wrong label | fix author/label |\n| `status=BLOCKED`, `blockerReason` mentions policy | Forge was correctly denied | do not loosen policy; decide as a human |\n| No `prUrl` but `SUCCESS` | PR creation not permitted (`allowPrCreation=false`) | expected in sandbox; ask operator |\n| Empty `changes` with a summary | task exceeded bounds or was ambiguous | split/sharpen the task (§4) |\n| Model route errors in `diagnosis` | free route rate-limited | retryable; re-run |\n| Audit finds nothing | excerpts capped; not a code-reading audit | request specific files or a coding task |\n\n---\n\n## 10. The handoff protocol\n\nMulti-party coordination happens through **`COORDINATION.md`** at the repo root. It is\n**append-only**. Every entry must carry: an **ID**, **timestamp (UTC)**, **author**, and\n**type** (`REPORT`, `QUESTION`, `ANSWER`, `DECISION`, `AUDIT`, `BLOCKER`, `TEST`).\n\nRules:\n- Never overwrite or delete previous entries.\n- To correct a mistake, append a new entry referencing the original ID.\n- **Never put secrets, tokens, or credentials in it.**\n- Cite raw evidence (commands, exit codes, run IDs), not adjectives.\n\n---\n\n## 11. Golden rules (memorise these)\n\n1. **One bounded task per mission.** Small and specific beats broad.\n2. **The report is the truth.** No evidence, no claim.\n3. **Never treat Forge's word as verification.** The Sentinel verifies; tests are the authority.\n4. **Never ask for merge or main access.** Those are reserved by design.\n5. **For an audit, verify paths and honour `observed` vs `inferred`.**\n6. **Respect a `BLOCKED` outcome.** It usually means the guardrail worked.\n7. **Record everything in `COORDINATION.md`** with IDs and raw evidence.\n8. **Never place secrets anywhere.** If a key appears, stop and flag it for revocation.\n\n---\n\n*This manual describes Forge as of commit `1fc748e` (main) plus the `forge/task-sentinel`\nand `forge/task-audit-brain` branches. Do not merely assign a fixed diagnosis based on the subject name.\n3. **Choose a teaching strategy** — adapt the explanation to the student's actual response and reasoning.\n4. **Teach** — give a clear, age-appropriate explanation grounded in the real lesson and curriculum.\n5. **Practice** — ask targeted questions and provide useful, varied practice.\n6. **Analyze reasoning** — inspect the student's answer and reasoning, not only whether the final answer is correct.\n7. **Recheck/adapt** — change the explanation or difficulty when evidence shows that the student has not understood; do not repeat an identical question as the only recovery strategy.\n8. **Verify outcome** — establish what the student can now do and record evidence.  "new_content": "/**\n * @license\n * SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\n */\n\nimport React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';\nimport { OfficialCurriculumLesson } from true,\n    'off_fr_u1_l1_salutations': true,\n    'off_math_u1_l1': true,\n    'off_mathfr_u1_l1_decimaux': true,\n    'off_sci_u1_l1_plant_needs': true,\n    'off_scifr_u1_l1_plantes': true,\n  });\n\n  const [activeTeachingLessonId, setActiveTeachingLessonId] = useState<string | null>(null);\n  const [activeStudyLesson, setActiveStudyLesson] = useState<OfficialCurriculumLesson | l.titleAr.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||\n          l.titleEn.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||\n          (l.titleFr && l.titleFr.toLowerCase().includes(q)) ||\n          l.subjectNameAr.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||\n          l.sourceRef.bookAr.toLowerCase().includes(q) ||\n          (l.readingText && l.readingText.toLowerCase().includes(q))\n      );\n    }\n    return list;\n  }, [officialLessons, selectedSubjectId, searchQuery]);\n\n  // Group lessons of current selected subject by unit\n  const activeSubjectUnits = useMemo(() => {\n    if   "body": "## Defect (P0 — runtime crash on a locked requirement)\n\nThe Library's **\"Learn with Nour\"** button (`src/components/curriculum/CurriculumBrowser.tsx:471`) called `setActiveStageLessonId(lesson.id)`. So the correct action is to navigate to the Nour tab:\n\n```diff\n-  setActiveStageLessonId(lesson.id);\n+  setActiveTab('companion');\n```\n\n`setActiveTab` and `setCompanionContext` are already imported from `useApp()`. No architecture change, no new dependency.\n\n## Verification (observed, on this branch)\n\n| Command | Before | After |\n|---|---|---|\n| `npm run lint` (`tsc --noEmit`) | 15 errors, incl. `TS2552` at line 471 | 14 errors — **the undefined identifier is gone**; the remaining 14 are pre-existing type-safety issues, unchanged |\n| `npm test` | — | adaptive 39/0, teaching, integrity **57/0** |\n| `GITHUB_PAGES=true npm run build` | — | exit 0 |\n\nNote: `npm install` without flags fails with `ERESOLVE` (vite@8 wants `esbuild@^0.27||^0.28`, root pins `^0.25`); used `--legacy-peer-deps`, the same flag the repo's own `deploy-pages.yml` uses. No lockfile is committed here.\n\n## Not in this PR\n\nThe 14 remaining `tsc` errors (null-safety in `teacherContextEngine.ts`, removed `DayRecord.lessons/.homework` in `CompanionChatScreen.tsx`, an `EvidenceModality` mismatch in `missionCompletion.ts`) are real but separate; fixing them would widen this change past the P0.\n\nDo not merge without owner approval.\n\n_This PR was created by an AI agent (OpenHands) on behalf of the user._",

For the failure modes that actually happened — a \"stored XSS\" claim with\n * no HTML sink anywhere, a \"hardcoded API key\" claim for a key read from the\n * environment — we settle the question deterministically by searching the real\n * source at the exact commit, and we show the command and its raw result so a\n * non-coder can spot-check it.\n *\n * The corpus is the exact-commit tarball, parsed in memory. No target code runs.\n */\nimport { gunzipSync } from 'node:zlib';\n\n/** Text/source extensions worth scanning; everything else is skipped. */\nconst TEXT_RE = /\\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs|json|md|yml|yaml|html|css|scss|txt|env|toml|sh|py|go|rb|java|kt)$/i;\n\n/** Raw-HTML sinks. If none exist, a \"stored XSS via rendering\" claim is false. */\nexport const RENDER_SINKS = [\n  'dangerouslySetInnerHTML',\n  'innerHTML',\n  'outerHTML',\n  'insertAdjacentHTML',\n  'document.write',\n  'eval(',\n  'new Function(',\n];\n\n/** Literal credentials. If none exist, a \"hardcoded secret\" claim is false. */\nexport const SECRET_LITERAL_RE =\n  /(AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\\-]{20,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,})/;\n\nexport interface EvidenceCheck {\n  /** What the check establishes, in plain words. */\n  claim: string;\n  /** A command a human can run to reproduce the check. */\n  command: string;\n  /** The raw result the check returned. */\n  result: string;\n  /** true = supports the finding; false = contradicts it. */\n  supports: boolean;\n  /** Literal a reader can paste into GitHub search to spot-check this themselves. */\n  needle?: string;\n}\n\nexport type FindingVerdict = 'SUPPORTED' | 'CONTRADICTED' | 'UNVERIFIED';\nexport type FindingCategory = 'verified-fact' | 'judgment';\n\nexport interface EvidenceOutcome {\n  verdict: FindingVerdict;\n  category: FindingCategory;\n  checks: EvidenceCheck[];\n}\n\n/** Parse a gzipped tar archive into a { relativePath: utf8Text } map. */\nexport function parseTarGz(gz: Buffer): Record<string, string> {\n  const buf = gunzipSync(gz);\n  const files: Record<string, string> = {};\n  let offset = 0;\n  let pendingName: string | null = null;\n\n  while (offset + 512 <= buf.length) {\n    const header = buf.subarray(offset, offset + 512);\n    if (header.every((b) => b === 0)) break; // end-of-archive marker\n    const name = readStr(header, 0, 100);\n    const size = Number.parseInt(readStr(header, 124, 12).trim() || '0', 8) || 0;\n    const typeflag = String.fromCharCode(header[156] || 48);\n    const prefix = readStr(header, 345, 155);\n    const dataStart = offset + 512;\n    const dataEnd = dataStart + size;\n\n    let fullName = pendingName ?? (prefix ? `${prefix}/${name}` : name);\n    pendingName = null;\n\n    if (typeflag === 'L') {\n      // GNU long name: this entry's data holds the *next* entry's path.\n      pendingName = readStr(buf.subarray(dataStart, dataEnd), 0, size);\n    } else if (typeflag === '0' || typeflag === '\\0') {\n      const rel = fullName.split('/').slice(1).join('/'); // drop the \"owner-repo-sha/\" root\n      if (rel && TEXT_RE.test(rel)) files[rel] = buf.subarray(dataStart, dataEnd).toString('utf8');\n    }\n    offset = dataStart + Math.ceil(size / 512) * 512;\n  }\n  return files;\n}\n\nfunction readStr(b: Uint8Array, off: number, len: number): string {\n  const slice = b.subarray(off, off + len);\n  const end = slice.indexOf(0);\n  return Buffer.from(end >= 0 ? slice.subarray(0, end) : slice).toString('utf8');\n}\n\nexport interface Hit {\n  path: string;\n  line: number;\n  text: string;\n}\n\n/** Find every line in the corpus containing `needle` (case-insensitive). */\nexport function searchCorpus(files: Record<string, string>, needle: string): Hit[] {\n  const hits: Hit[] = [];\n  const n = needle.toLowerCase();\n  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {\n    content.split('\\n').forEach((text, i) => {\n      if (text.toLowerCase().includes(n)) hits.push({ path, line: i + 1, text: text.trim().slice(0, 140) });\n    });\n  }\n  return hits;\n}\n\n/** Aggregate hits for several needles. */\nexport function searchMany(files: Record<string, string>, needles: string[]): Hit[] {\n  return needles.flatMap((n) => searchCorpus(files, n));\n}\n\nexport function isRenderSinkClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  return /\\b(xss|cross[- ]site|unsanitized|raw html|innerhtml|dangerouslysetinnerhtml|html injection)\\b/i.test(text);\n}\n\nexport function isHardcodedSecretClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  const aboutSecret = /\\b(key|secret|token|password|credential)\\b/i.test(text);\n  const hardcoded = /\\b(hard[- ]?coded|committed|checked in|in the (source|code|repo|bundle))\\b/i.test(text);\n  return aboutSecret && hardcoded;\n}\n\nexport function isLockfileClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  return /\\b(lock ?file|package-lock|yarn\\.lock|pnpm-lock|shrinkwrap|deterministic (build|install)|reproducible (build|install))\\b/i.test(text);\n}\n\nexport function isApiKeyStatusClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  return /\\bhasapikey\\b/i.test(text) || (/\\bhealth\\b/i.test(text) && /\\bapi ?key\\b/i.test(text) && /\\b(expos|leak|disclos|reveal|presence|status|public)\\b/i.test(text));\n}\n\nexport function isLegacyPeerDepsClaim(text: string): boolean {\n  return /\\blegacy[- ]peer[- ]deps\\b/i.test(text);\n}\n\nconst LOCKFILE_NEEDLES = ['package-lock.json', 'yarn.lock', 'pnpm-lock.yaml', 'npm-shrinkwrap.json', 'bun.lock'];\n\n/**\n * Settle a finding deterministically against the real source.\n *\n * Each check is a question with a yes/no answer that the corpus can decide: does a\n * raw-HTML sink exist? does a lockfile exist? is a literal credential committed? does\n * a named string appear? A check that *confirms* a finding yields `verified-fact`;\n * one that *refutes* it yields `CONTRADICTED`; a claim none of these can address\n * stays an explicit `judgment`, never presented as a proven fact.\n */\nexport function verifyFinding(\n  finding: { title: string; evidence: string; recommendation: string; paths: string[] },\n  corpus: Record<string, string>,\n  fileCount: number\n): EvidenceOutcome {\n  const text = `${finding.title} ${finding.evidence} ${finding.recommendation}`;\n  const checks: EvidenceCheck[] = [];\n\n  const citedExist = finding.paths.length > 0;\n  checks.push({\n    claim: 'the cited paths exist in the repository',\n    command: `git ls-files | grep -F <path>`,\n    result: citedExist ? `all cited paths present: ${finding.paths.join(', ')}` : 'no path cited',\n    supports: citedExist,\n    needle: finding.paths[0],\n  });\n\n  const settle = (supports: boolean): EvidenceOutcome => ({\n    verdict: supports ? 'SUPPORTED' : 'CONTRADICTED',\n    category: 'verified-fact',\n    checks,\n  });\n\n  if (isRenderSinkClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, RENDER_SINKS);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'an unsafe HTML sink exists that could render untrusted content',\n      command: `grep -rn \"${RENDER_SINKS.join('|')}\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : `0 matches across ${fileCount} files`,\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isHardcodedSecretClaim(text)) {\n    const literal = Object.entries(corpus).flatMap(([path, content]) => {\n      const m = content.match(SECRET_LITERAL_RE);\n      return m ? [{ path }] : [];\n    });\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a literal credential is present in the source',\n      command: `grep -rEn \"${SECRET_LITERAL_RE.source.slice(0, 40)}…\" <repo>`,\n      result: literal.length ? `${literal.length} literal(s), e.g. ${literal[0].path}` : `0 literals across ${fileCount} files`,\n      supports: literal.length > 0,\n      needle: 'process.env',\n    });\n    return settle(literal.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLockfileClaim(text)) {\n    const present = LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.filter((n) => corpus[n] !== undefined);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a package-manager lockfile is present in the repository',\n      command: `git ls-files | grep -E \"${LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.join('|')}\"`,\n      result: present.length ? `present: ${present.join(', ')}` : `none of ${LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.join(', ')} (${fileCount} files)`,\n      supports: present.length === 0, // the finding asserts a lockfile is *missing*\n      needle: 'package-lock.json',\n    });\n    return settle(present.length === 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isApiKeyStatusClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['hasApiKey']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the source exposes whether an API key is configured',\n      command: `grep -rn \"hasApiKey\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'hasApiKey',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLegacyPeerDepsClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['legacy-peer-deps']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the CI workflow installs with --legacy-peer-deps',\n      command: `grep -rn \"legacy-peer-deps\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'legacy-peer-deps',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  return { verdict: 'UNVERIFIED', category: 'judgment', checks };\n}"

```ts
/** Files worth a syntax scan (TS/JS source only). */
const SOURCE_RE = /\.(ts|tsx|js|jsx|mjs|cjs)$/i;

const IDENTIFIER_RE = /[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*/g;
const CALL_RE = /(^|[^.\w$])([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*\(/g;

/** Reserved words and common globals that are not declared in-file. */
const GLOBALS = new Set([
  // JS/TS keywords that can precede "("
  'if','for','while','switch','catch','return','typeof','new','function','await','yield','else','do','try','case','delete','void','in','of','instanceof','throw','with','super','this','class','extends','import','export','default','const','let','var','async','static','get','set','as','satisfies','keyof','infer','readonly','namespace','declare','abstract','enum','implements','interface','type','is',
  // global functions/objects
  'Array','Object','String','Number','Boolean','Symbol','BigInt','Math','JSON','Date','RegExp','Error','TypeError','RangeError','SyntaxError','ReferenceError','EvalError','URIError','AggregateError','Promise','Map','Set','WeakMap','WeakSet','Proxy','Reflect','Intl','BigInt64Array','BigUint64Array','Float32Array','Float64Array','Int8Array','Int16Array','Int32Array','Uint8Array','Uint8ClampedArray','Uint16Array','Uint32Array','ArrayBuffer','SharedArrayBuffer','DataView','Atomics','structuredClone','queueMicrotask',
  'parseInt','parseFloat','isNaN','isFinite','encodeURIComponent','decodeURIComponent','encodeURI','decodeURI','escape','unescape','eval','fetch','setTimeout','setInterval','clearTimeout','clearInterval','setImmediate','clearImmediate','requestAnimationFrame','cancelAnimationFrame','atob','btoa','alert','confirm','prompt','print','require','define',
  // TS utility types (rarely called, but safe)
  'Partial','Required','Readonly','Record','Pick','Omit','Exclude','Extract','NonNullable','Parameters','ReturnType','InstanceType','Awaited','Uppercase','Lowercase','Capitalize','Uncapitalize',
]);

/** Locally-declared names: declarations, params, imports, catch bindings, class/type names. */
function declaredNames(code: string): Set<string> {
  const names = new Set<string>();
  const add = (s: string | undefined) => { if (s) names.add(s); };
  const collectList = (list: string) => {
    for (const m of list.matchAll(IDENTIFIER_RE)) add(m[0]);
  };
  // import ... from  |  import X, {a as b} from
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\bimport\b[\s\S]*?\bfrom\b/g)) {
    const clause = m[0].replace(/\bimport\b/, '').replace(/\bfrom\b[\s\S]*$/, '');
    collectList(clause);
  }
  // function/class/const/let/var/enum/interface/type/namespace declarations
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\b(?:function|class|interface|type|enum|namespace|module)\s+([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)/g)) add(m[1]);
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\b(?:const|let|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)/g)) add(m[1]);
  // destructuring in const/let/var { a, b: c } =  and [a, b] =
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\b(?:const|let|var)\s*([\[{][\s\S]*?[\]}])\s*=/g)) collectList(m[1]);
  // function params: capture ( ... ) after function name or arrow
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\bfunction\s*[A-Za-z0-9_$]*\s*\(([^)]*)\)/g)) collectList(m[1]);
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\(([^)]*)\)\s*=>/g)) collectList(m[1]);
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\b([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*=>/g)) add(m[1]);
  // class methods: name(...) {  — capture method params
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\b(?:public|private|protected|static|async|get|set|\s)+([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\s*\(([^)]*)\)/g)) collectList(m[2]);
  // catch (e)
  for (const m of code.matchAll(/\bcatch\s*\(([^)]*)\)/g)) collectList(m[1]);
  // object property shorthand / keys and named function params in object types — too broad; skip
  return names;
}
```

export function findUndefinedIdentifiers(files: Record<string,string>): Hit[] {
  const hits: Hit[] = [];
  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {
    if (!SOURCE_RE.test(path)) continue;
    const declared = declaredNames(content);
    for (const m of content.matchAll(CALL_RE)) {
      const name = m[2];
      if (GLOBALS.has(name) || declared.has(name)) continue;
      const idx = (m.index ?? 0) + m[0].length - m[2].length - 1; // position of name
      const line = content.slice(0, m.index! + m[0].indexOf(name)).split('\n').length;
      const text = content.split('\n')[line-1]?.trim().slice(0,140) ?? '';
      hits.push({ path, line, text, name } as Hit & {name:string});
    }
  }
  return hits;
}

'SUPPORTED' : 'CONTRADICTED',\n    category: 'verified-fact',\n    checks,\n  });\n\n  if (isRenderSinkClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, RENDER_SINKS);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'an unsafe HTML sink exists that could render untrusted content',\n      command: `grep -rn \"${RENDER_SINKS.join('|')}\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : `0 matches across ${fileCount} files`,\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isHardcodedSecretClaim(text)) {\n    const literal = Object.entries(corpus).flatMap(([path, content]) => {\n      const m = content.match(SECRET_LITERAL_RE);\n      return m ? [{ path }] : [];\n    });\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a literal credential is present in the source',\n      command: `grep -rEn \"${SECRET_LITERAL_RE.source.slice(0, 40)}…\" <repo>`,\n      result: literal.length ? `${literal.length} literal(s), e.g. ${literal[0].path}` : `0 literals across ${fileCount} files`,\n      supports: literal.length > 0,\n      needle: 'process.env',\n    });\n    return settle(literal.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLockfileClaim(text)) {\n    const present = LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.filter((n) => corpus[n] !== undefined);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a package-manager lockfile is present in the repository',\n      command: `git ls-files | grep -E \"${LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.join('|')}\"`,\n      result: present.length ? `present: ${present.join(', ')}` : `none of ${LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.join(', ')} (${fileCount} files)`,\n      supports: present.length === 0, // the finding asserts a lockfile is *missing*\n      needle: 'package-lock.json',\n    });\n    return settle(present.length === 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isApiKeyStatusClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['hasApiKey']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the source exposes whether an API key is configured',\n      command: `grep -rn \"hasApiKey\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'hasApiKey',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLegacyPeerDepsClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['legacy-peer-deps']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the CI workflow installs with --legacy-peer-deps',\n      command: `grep -rn \"legacy-peer-deps\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'legacy-peer-deps',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  return { verdict: 'UNVERIFIED', category: 'judgment', checks };\n}\n",

function stripCommentsAndStrings(code) {
  let out = '';
  let i = 0;
  const n = code.length;
  while (i < n) {
    const c = code[i], d = code[i+1];
    if (c === '/' && d === '/') { // line comment
      while (i < n && code[i] !== '\n') i++;
      continue;
    }
    if (c === '/' && d === '*') { // block comment
      i += 2;
      while (i < n && !(code[i] === '*' && code[i+1] === '/')) i++;
      i += 2;
      continue;
    }
    if (c === '"' || c === "'" || c === '`') {
      const q = c; i++;
      while (i < n) {
        if (code[i] === '\\') { i += 2; continue; }
        if (code[i] === q) { i++; break; }
        if (q === '`' && code[i] === '$' && code[i+1] === '{') {
          // skip balanced braces in template expression
          i += 2; let depth = 1;
          while (i < n && depth > 0) { if (code[i] === '{') depth++; else if (code[i] === '}') depth--; i++; }
          continue;
        }
        i++;
      }
      out += ' '; // replace string with a space
      continue;
    }
    out += c; i++;
  }
  return out;
}

```ts
const DEFN_RE = /\b(?:function|class|interface|type|enum|namespace|module|declare|abstract|public|private|protected|static|get|set)\b/;

export function findUndefinedIdentifiers(files) {
  const hits = [];
  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {
    if (!SOURCE_RE.test(path)) continue;
    const code = stripCommentsAndStrings(content);
    // Count every identifier mention so a name that is declared (or imported, or used
    // more than once) is trusted, and only a name that appears exactly once is suspect.
    const counts = new Map();
    for (const m of code.matchAll(IDENTIFIER_RE)) counts.set(m[0], (counts.get(m[0])||0)+1);
    const lines = content.split('\n');
    for (const m of code.matchAll(CALL_RE)) {
      const name = m[2];
      if (GLOBALS.has(name)) continue;
      if ((counts.get(name) ?? 0) !== 1) continue;      // declared/imported/used elsewhere
      const nameStart = m.index! + m[1].length;
      if (code.slice(nameStart, m.index! + m[0].length).includes('\n')) continue;
      const line = code.slice(0, nameStart).split('\n').length;
      const text = (lines[line-1] ?? '').trim();
      // Skip definitions/keyword contexts (function, class, new, public, …).
      const before = code.slice(Math.max(0, nameStart - 40), nameStart);
      if (DEFN_RE.test(before) || /\bnew\s+$/.test(before)) continue;
      hits.push({ path, line, text: text.slice(0,140), name });
    }
  }
  return hits;
}
```

Good: the buggy version correctly detects `setActiveStageLessonId` at 471. But there are 56 false positives, mostly interface method signatures (`getStudent(): Promise<...>;`) and `constructor()`. 

The issue: interface method signatures like `getStudent(studentId: string): Promise<Student | null>;` — the name `getStudent` appears once (declared as a method signature; it's not a call). My heuristic counts it once and flags it. I need to exclude method *declarations/signatures*.

Why does the "count===1" not save these? Because interface methods are declared once (signature only) and never called within the interface file. So they appear once → flagged.

I need to exclude a `name(...)` that is a declaration/signature rather than a call. Distinguishing factors:
- Signature: `name(params): ReturnType;` or `name(params) {` (method definition) — the `(` is followed (after balanced parens) by `:` or `{` or `;`.
- Call: `name(args)` followed by `;`, `)`, `,`, `.`, `}` etc., but NOT immediately a `:` type.

Hmm. The reliable distinguishing feature: after the balanced closing paren, a method *definition* has `{` or `: Type {`; an interface *signature* has `: Type ;`. A call never has `: Type` after it (except ternary? `cond ? f() : g()` — but that has a space and is `?`-context; actually `f() : ...` in ternary is `f() ? a : b`). A call result followed by `:` is rare. So: if after the closing paren (skipping whitespace) comes `:` and then a type and then `;`/`{`, treat as signature/definition.

But also `constructor() {` is a method definition (followed by `{`). And arrow `const x = () =>` handled separately.

So the rule: find the matching close paren for the call; look at the next non-space char:
- `{` → method/function body → definition, skip.
- `:` → could be signature `: Type;` or `: Type {` → skip (calls don't produce `: Type`).
- `=>` → arrow definition, skip.
- else → call.

But careful: a call inside a ternary/object... e.g., `onClick={() => {` no. `{ onPress: foo() }`? The `:` is *before* foo, not after. After `foo()` is `}`. Fine. What about `f() : x`? Only ternary `cond ? f() : x` — here after `f()` is ` : x`. That would be misclassified as signature. But that's rare and would be a false negative (missing a real bug) — acceptable per precision-over-recall.

Also `constructor()` — followed by `{` → skip. Good.

Let me also handle: a call `name(...)` followed by `;` where name is a single-occurrence interface signature WITHOUT a return type: `foo();` in an interface? Interfaces always have return types or `void`. Method signatures in interfaces always have `:`. And abstract methods too. So `:` rule covers them.

But what about type-level function property: `onClick?: () => void` — `onClick` not followed by `(`. `handler: (e) => void` no name-paren. `foo: () => void` no. `foo(): void;` covered by `:`.

Let me implement matching-paren logic:

```
function matchParen(code, openIdx) {
  let depth=0;
  for (let i=openIdx;i<code.length;i++){
    if(code[i]==='(')depth++;
    else if(code[i]===')'){depth--; if(depth===0)return i;}
  }
  return -1;

}\n  return hits;\n}\n\n/** Aggregate hits for several needles. */\nexport function searchMany(files: Record<string, string>, needles: string[]): Hit[] {\n  return needles.flatMap((n) => return /\\b(lock ?file|package-lock|yarn\\.lock|pnpm-lock|shrinkwrap|deterministic (build|install)|reproducible (build|install))\\b/i.test(text);\n}\n\nexport function isApiKeyStatusClaim(text: string/template literals, preserving length and newlines so\n * reported line numbers still match the original file. '\\n' : ' ');\n  let i = 0;\n  while (i < n) {\n    const c = code[i];\n    const d = code[i + 1];\n    if (c === '/' && d === '/') {\n      while (i < n && code[i] !== '\\n') push(code[i++]);\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (c === '/' && d === '*') {\n      push(code[i++]); push(code[i++]);\n      while (i < n && !(code[i] === '*' && code[i + 1] === '/')) push(code[i++]);\n      if (i < n) { push(code[i++]); push(code[i++]); }\n      continue;\n    }\n    if (c === '\"' || c === \"'\" || c === '`') {\n      const q = c;\n      push(code[i++]);\n      while (i < n) {\n        if (code[i] === '\\\\') { push(code[i++]); if (i < n) push(code[i++]); continue; }\n        if (code[i] === q) { push(code[i++]); break; }\n        if (q === '`' && code[i] === '$' && code[i + 1] === '{') {\n          let depth = 0;\n          do {\n            if (code[i] === '{') depth++;\n            else if (code[i] === '}') depth--;\n            push(code[i++]);\n          } while (i < n && depth > 0);\n          continue;\n        }\n        push(code[i++]);\n      }\n      continue;\n    }\n    out.push(c);\n    i++;\n  }\n  return out.join('');\n}\n\n/** Keywords that can immediately precede a name that is a definition, not a call. */\nconst DEFN_KEYWORDS = new Set([\n  'function', 'class', 'interface', 'type', 'enum', 'namespace', 'module', 'declare', 'abstract',\n  'public', 'private', 'protected', 'static', 'get', 'set', 'new', 'async', 'extends', 'implements',\n  'export', 'default', 'return', 'typeof', 'void', 'delete', 'await', 'yield', 'case', 'in', 'of',\n  'instanceof', 'else', 'do', 'throw',\n]);\n\nexport interface UndefinedHit extends Hit {\n  name: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * Static scan for calls to names that are neither declared, imported, nor referenced\n * anywhere else in their own file. Such a call throws a ReferenceError the moment that\n * code path runs — a real runtime defect a pure read-only audit otherwise cannot see,\n * because it never executes the target and its evidence checks only ask whether cited\n * paths exist.\n *\n * Precision over recall, and never executing the target: comments and string literals are\n * stripped first; a name is only reported when it is written as a call, is not a standard\n * global, is not preceded by a definition keyword, and appears exactly once in the file\n * (a real symbol is always declared, imported, or used more than once). This deliberately\n * misses cases rather than inventing them.\n */\n/** Index of the `)` matching the `(` at `openIdx`, or -1. */\nfunction matchingParen(code: string, openIdx: number): number {\n  let depth = 0;\n  for (let i = openIdx; i < code.length; i++) {\n    if (code[i] === '(') depth++;\n    else if (code[i] === ')') {\n      depth--;\n      if (depth === 0) return i;\n    }\n  }\n  return -1;\n}\n\nexport function findUndefinedIdentifiers(files: Record<string, string>): UndefinedHit[] {\n  const hits: UndefinedHit[] = [];\n  for (const [path, content] of Object.entries(files)) {\n    if (!SOURCE_RE.test(path)) continue;\n    const code = stripCommentsAndStrings(content);\n    const counts = new Map<string, number>();\n    for (const m of code.matchAll(IDENTIFIER_RE)) counts.set(m[0], (counts.get(m[0]) ?? 0) + 1);\n    const lines = content.split('\\n');\n    for (const m of code.matchAll(CALL_RE)) {\n      const name = m[2];\n      if (GLOBALS.has(name) || (counts.get(name) ?? 0) !== 1) continue;\n      const nameStart = m.index! + m[1].length;\n      const parenIdx = nameStart + name.length;\n      // `name(` split across lines is a signature/parameter continuation, never a call.\n      if (code.slice(nameStart, parenIdx).includes('\\n')) continue;\n      const close = matchingParen(code, parenIdx);\n      if (close < 0) continue;\n      // A definition or signature — `name(...) {`, `name(...): Type`, `name(...) =>` — is\n      // not a call; a call is never immediately followed by a body, a return type, or `=>`.\n      let j = close + 1;\n      while (j < code.length && /\\s/.test(code[j])) j++;\n      if (code[j] === '{' || code[j] === ':' || code.slice(j, j + 2) === '=>') continue;\n      const before = code.slice(0, nameStart);\n      const prevWord = before.match(/([A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*)\\s*$/)?.[1] ?? '';\n      if (DEFN_KEYWORDS.has(prevWord)) continue;\n      const line = before.split('\\n').length;\n      hits.push({ path, line, text: (lines[line - 1] ?? '').trim().slice(0, 140), name });\n    }\n  }\n  return hits;\n}\n\nconst LOCKFILE_NEEDLES = ['package-lock.json', 'yarn.lock', 'pnpm-lock.yaml', 'npm-shrinkwrap.json', 'bun.lock'];\n\n/**\n * Settle a finding deterministically against the real source.\n *\n * Each check is a question with a yes/no answer that the corpus can decide: does a\n * raw-HTML sink exist? does a lockfile exist? is a literal credential committed? does\n * a named string appear? [{ path }] : [];\n    });\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a literal credential is present in the source',\n      command: `grep -rEn \"${SECRET_LITERAL_RE.source.slice(0, 40)}…\" <repo>`,\n      result: literal.length ? `${literal.length} literal(s), e.g. ${literal[0].path}` : `0 literals across ${fileCount} files`,\n      supports: literal.length > 0,\n      needle: 'process.env',\n    });\n    return settle(literal.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLockfileClaim(text)) {\n    const present = LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.filter((n) => corpus[n] !== undefined);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a package-manager lockfile is present in the repository',\n      command: `git ls-files | grep -E \"${LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.join('|')}\"`,\n      result: present.length ? `present: ${present.join(', ')}` : `none of ${LOCKFILE_NEEDLES.join(', ')} (${fileCount} files)`,\n      supports: present.length === 0, // the finding asserts a lockfile is *missing*\n      needle: 'package-lock.json',\n    });\n    return settle(present.length === 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isApiKeyStatusClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['hasApiKey']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the source exposes whether an API key is configured',\n      command: `grep -rn \"hasApiKey\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'hasApiKey',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLegacyPeerDepsClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['legacy-peer-deps']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the CI workflow installs with --legacy-peer-deps',\n      command: `grep -rn \"legacy-peer-deps\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'legacy-peer-deps',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  return { verdict: 'UNVERIFIED', category: 'judgment', checks };\n}\n",

i < code.length; i++) {\n    if (code[i] === '(') depth++;\n    else if (code[i] === ')') {\n      depth--;\n      if (depth === 0) return i;\n    }\n  }\n  return -1;\n}\n\n/**\n * Static scan for calls to names that are neither declared, imported, nor referenced\n * anywhere else in their own file. [{ path }] : [];\n    });\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'a literal credential is present in the source',\n      command: `grep -rEn \"${SECRET_LITERAL_RE.source.slice(0, 40)}…\" <repo>`,\n      result: literal.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'hasApiKey',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  if (isLegacyPeerDepsClaim(text)) {\n    const hits = searchMany(corpus, ['legacy-peer-deps']);\n    checks.push({\n      claim: 'the CI workflow installs with --legacy-peer-deps',\n      command: `grep -rn \"legacy-peer-deps\" <repo>`,\n      result: hits.length ? `${hits.length} match(es), e.g. ${hits[0].path}:${hits[0].line}` : '0 matches',\n      supports: hits.length > 0,\n      needle: 'legacy-peer-deps',\n    });\n    return settle(hits.length > 0);\n  }\n\n  return { verdict: 'UNVERIFIED', category: 'judgment', checks };\n}\n",

'';\n      if (DEFN_KEYWORDS.has(prevWord)) continue;\n      const line = before.split('\\n').length;\n      hits.push({ path, line, text: (lines[line - 1] ?? stub. */\nfunction tarEntry(name: string, content: string): Buffer {\n  const data = Buffer.from(content, 'utf8');\n  const header = Buffer.alloc(512);\n  header.write(name, 0, 100, 'utf8');\n  header.write('0000644\\0', 100, 8, 'utf8');\n  header.write('0000000\\0', 108, 8, 'utf8');\n  header.write('0000000\\0', 116, 8, 'utf8');\n  header.write(data.length.toString(8).padStart(11, '0') + '\\0', 124, 12, 'utf8');\n  header.write('00000000000\\0', 136, 12, 'utf8');\n  header.write('        ', 148, 8, 'utf8'); // checksum placeholder (spaces)\n  header.write('0', 156, 1, 'utf8');\n  header.write('ustar\\0', 257, 6, 'utf8');\n  header.write('00', 263, 2, 'utf8');\n  let sum = 0;\n  for (const b of header) sum += b;\n  header.write(sum.toString(8).padStart(6, '0') + '\\0 ', 148, 8, 'utf8');\n  const pad = Buffer.alloc((512 - (data.length % 512)) % 512);\n  return Buffer.concat([header, data, pad]);\n}\n\nfunction tarGz(files: Record<string, string>): Buffer {\n  const parts = `Registry latest: ${checked.map((d) => `${d.name} ${grounder.get(d.name)!.latest}`).join(', ')}.`\n      : 'No dependency version claims were made.',\n    ...(grounded.notes.length ? grounded.notes : ['No version claim was contradicted by the registry.']),\n  ];\n\n  // ---- Evidence: settle what we can mechanically, and label the rest judgment. ----\n  const corpus = options.corpus !== undefined ? options.corpus : await fetchRepoCorpus(options.ctx.target, options.ctx.commit);\n  const evidence: Record<string, EvidenceOutcome> = {};\n  if (corpus) {\n    for (const f of findings) evidence[f.title] = verifyFinding(f, corpus, Object.keys(corpus).length);\n  }\n  const evidenceSummary = {\n    verified: Object.values(evidence).filter((e) => e.verdict === 'SUPPORTED').length,\n    contradicted: Object.values(evidence).filter((e) => e.verdict === 'CONTRADICTED').length,\n    judgment: findings.length - Object.values(evidence).filter((e) => e.verdict !== 'UNVERIFIED').length,\n  };\n\n  // ---- Phase 2: Forge synthesizes, then the panel verifies. ----\n  const phase2 = await runCompany({\n    goal: `Synthesize and verify the audit of ${options.ctx.target}`,\n    plan: () => [\n      { id: 'synthesis', title: 'Forge lead synthesis' },\n      { id: 'verify', title: 'Verification panel' },\n    ],\n    rosterFor: (item) =>\n      item.id === 'synthesis'\n        ? [leadRole(options.model, options.ctx, findings, recorder)]\n        : VERIFY_PANEL.map((name) => verifierRole(options.model, name, options.ctx, findings, recorder)),\n    attemptsPerItem: 1,\n    maxRoleRuns: 8,\n    rubric: [\n      { name: 'completed', points: 3, mandatory: true, test: ({ run }) => run.status === 'COMPLETED' },\n      { name: 'has-synthesis', points: 2, test: (ctx) => Boolean((ctx.bus.latest(ctx.attempt, 'note')?.data?.summary as string | undefined)?.trim()) },\n    ],\n    integrate: () => ({ ok: true, reason: 'audit is read-only' }),\n  });\n\n  const synthesisArtifact = phase2.bus.latest('synthesis#1', 'note');\n  const synthesis = {\n    summary: String(synthesisArtifact?.data?.summary ?? ''),\n    architecture: String(synthesisArtifact?.data?.architecture ?? '').toUpperCase();\n      const verdict: 'CONFIRM' | 'OBJECT' | 'UNVERIFIED' = raw === 'OBJECT' ? 'OBJECT' : raw === 'CONFIRM' ?
